items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 音乐厅完成了一次两小时的无脚本独奏即兴录音，专辑《Sendas》以这段原始音频为素材，后期混入人声采样、打击乐、循环音效、田野录音与拾得声音。作为受 Thelonious Monk '绝不重复' 精神影响的创作，Sosa 拒绝被归类于爵士、拉丁或古典等任何风格框架，强调'无错音符'与'少即是多'的美学。专辑诞生于疫情封锁与个人婚姻变动的特殊时期，在空旷音乐厅中以法齐奥里三角钢琴的共鸣为核心，探索声音的物理质感与精神维度，呈现出冥想式、不断生成的音乐旅程。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这不是传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是一组来自芝加哥南区的田野录音档案。由录音师Ian Brennan操刀，二十五位遭受枪支暴力影响的居民在前廊讲述亲身经历，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。文中明确指出没有添加任何音乐成分，所有声音均来自现场。一位母亲在讲述失去孩子的经过时反复说'对不起，对不起，对不起'，她的崩溃成为整张作品最具冲击力的时刻。录音地点位于中城机场降落路径正下方的街区，恰逢特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队的那一天。专辑收益将捐赠给以公共卫生方法遏制暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。这是一份关于芝加哥南区真实声音的文献记录，与实验音乐、田野录音、社会声学等创作脉络在方法论上有相通之处。

items.body: EYAA takes its name from a cry of encouragement tied to trance. The French-Ghanaian trio put out “Luku Luku” on Sharma Records on 2 October, the first of five singles leading to their first EP. The voice is Kyekyeku‘s, a singer and guitarist from Accra who now lives in Bayonne, in south-west France, and has worked with highlife veterans Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor. He formed the seven-piece Ah! Kwantou in 2019, and two of its members, bassist Kevin Bucquet and drummer Fred Faure, are the other two thirds of EYAA. In EYAA, Bucquet plays synths and runs the machines as well as the bass, and he, Faure and Kyekyeku composed “Luku Luku” together, with Kyekyeku writing the words. Kyekyeku sings in Twi, pidgin and English over Faure’s drums and Bucquet’s bass, with synths and machines adding the electronics, and the grooves draw on afro-funk, highlife and afrobeat to make an afro-electro built for dancing. This year the trio has played in France, in Accra at Les Francophonies Festival, and in Portugal at Tom de Festa Festival in Tondela. Listen to “Luku Luku” HERE The post Daily Discovery: LUKU LUKU – EYAA appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — The third album of my beloved Procol Harum, "A salty dog". The last one with Dave Knights on bass guitar and the last one as well with Matthew Fisher on keys, who he also did the production on this one. Now, "A salty dog", is a much more laid-back record than the two previous of the band, yet is so so beautiful. Mostly blues-based with a progressive direction, and always having the distinctive Procol Harum sound, meaning piano and voice driven. When Gary Brooker first performed the piece "A salty dog" on piano, the room was filled with sunlight shining through the windows. The drummer, B.J. Wilson, with a sunbeam on his face, told Brooker he thought it was the most beautiful song he had ever heard. Gary Brooker delivers some vein-cutting vocals throughout the album. Matthew Fisher did the lead vocals on three tracks on this one, "Boredom", "Wreck of the Hesperus" and "Pilgrim's progress". The track "Crucifiction" is a lament with ripping lead vocals provided by Robin Trower. A really beautiful album, closing a chapter for Procol Harum.
items._genre: crossover prog / blues rock / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Procol Harum第三张专辑，被认为是乐队向更舒缓方向转变的代表作。专辑以蓝调为根基，融入渐进摇滚的结构感，延续了乐队标志性的钢琴与人声主导风格。Gary Brooker的演唱贯穿全篇，情感浓烈而富有穿透力；Matthew Fisher在三首曲目中担任主唱，Robin Trower则在一首挽歌式的作品中献上撕裂的主音人声。整体制作偏向内敛与氛围营造，与乐队前两张作品相比张力有所减弱，但旋律与编曲的精致程度依然突出。该专辑也标志着贝斯手Dave Knights与键盘手Matthew Fisher在乐队时代的终结，具有承上启下的意义。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — The progressive metal movement, whose foundations were first laid in the mid-to-late 1980s by pioneers such as Queensr�che, Fates Warning, and Dream Theater, gained a much stronger identity and momentum during the 1990s, eventually expanding and establishing itself as a fully-fledged genre in the 2000s. Redemption belongs to the group of bands that emerged under that inspiring influence, shaping a powerful and virtuosic musical approach, immersed in the intricate structures of the most contemporary prog metal.With their self-titled 2003 debut album, Redemption had already shown what they were capable of, although it was still a somewhat raw and unpolished power-metal-style offering with nascent progressive elements. For "The Fullness of Time" (2005), their second album, the band led by Nick van Dyk brought in the duo James Sherwood (bass) and Chris Quirarte (drums), both from the ranks of the Los Angeles-based band Prymary, as their new rhythm section, and, most importantly, vocalist Ray Alder -who also fronted Fates Warning- evolving toward a more defined and mature sound.The first third of the album retains the band's seminal sound, with machine-gun-like, galloping riffs; frenzied, counterpointing solos between Bernie Versailles and van Dyk; and Quirarte's wild double-bass drumming, to which van Dyk's keyboards add an additional, fitting melodic and atmospheric layer, both on the aggressive "Threads," the fast-paced "Scarred," and the reflective and bitter "Parker's Eyes" -which offers a somber and disheartening view of the world, including a reference to the events of 9/11- and incorporates a beautiful, arpeggiated acoustic nuance before exploding instrumentally.The following two-thirds reflect the band's solidity and progressive character, with the epic "Sapphire", a powerful and expansive instrumental tapestry led by a spirited Alder on vocals and generous with guitar and synthesizer solos, contrasted with calm, refreshing passages -the jewel of the album- and the intricate "The Fullness of Time," a suite divided into four sections where journeys through rocky peaks -the furious and vengeful "i. Rage" and the resilient "iii. Release"- alternate with clear, evocative sonic valleys -the meditative "ii. Despair" and the hopeful and luminous "iv. Trascendence"."The Fullness of Time" marked a turning point in Redemption's career: an album in which the band left behind the rough edges of its debut to find its own identity, delivering one of the genre's strongest offerings of the mid-2000s.4/4.5 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / heavy metal
items._cn_summary: 这张2005年发行的专辑是Redemption乐队从首作粗糙本色向成熟风格过渡的关键作品。乐队从洛杉矶Prymary引入新贝斯与鼓手，并邀请Fates Warning主唱Ray Alder加盟，使声音从萌芽期的前卫元素转向更完整的体系。专辑前三分之一保留了种子期特征：机枪式连复段、加倍鼓点的高速节奏、双吉他对位独奏与键盘的旋律氛围层交织。标题曲被分为四个乐章，在愤怒与绝望、释放与超越之间构建起伏的史诗段落，长篇器乐编织与抒情段落交替。整张专辑在前卫金属框架内融合了力量金属的冲击感与器乐独奏的炫目技巧，呈现出从早期粗砺走向独立辨识度的过程，是该流派2000年代中期较有分量的作品之一。

items.body: Virgin Birth, an industrial punk trio from Louisville, Kentucky, will release the six-song EP The Dead End on 16 October 2026 via Never Nervous Records. The band recorded the EP at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio in Louisville. The title track became available on streaming platforms on 2 October 2026, ahead of the full release. Virgin Birth is Phillip Olympia (vocals, synthesizers), Jake Miller (guitar) and Matt Haas (bass). Never Nervous Records described “The Dead End” as continuing the band’s “fascination with the darker corners of electronic music, punk, and the increasingly stupid world we all find ourselves living in.” The label said the band’s earlier releases “looked outward at collapse on a larger scale,” while the new songs are “more immediate, claustrophobic, and personal.” A music video for the title track is set to follow within the week, according to Never Nervous Records. “The Dead End” arrives digitally across major streaming platforms. More live dates and physical releases are planned through Never Nervous Records. About Virgin Birth Virgin Birth formed in Louisville as an industrial synth punk project led by Phillip Olympia and Jake Miller. The duo released its debut EP, “The Forest,” on 26 May 2023 through Never Nervous Records. The nine-track EP included backing vocals from Mandy Keathley and cover art by Albie Mason, and was mixed and mastered by Jake Miller at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio. Virgin Birth followed with the three-song EP “From Behind” on 14 April 2024, also recorded at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio. The band released “I Can’t Read” as a single in March 2025 ahead of its debut full-length album, “Total Annihilation,” issued 2 May 2025 via Never Nervous Records on digital formats and cassette. The ten-track album was again mixed and mastered by Jake Miller at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio, with Olympia handling vocals, synthesizers, drum machines and guitars, and Miller on guitars and synthesizers. Virgin Birth released the remix single “Don’t Tell Me [neu flesh remix]” in August 2025, followed the next month by “SPLIT,” a split release with Scary Black. Matt Haas joined the band on bass by June 2026, when Virgin Birth released a cover of Nirvana’s “Floyd the Barber” as a trio for the first time. “The Dead End” is Virgin Birth’s first EP since “From Behind” in 2024.
items._genre: industrial punk / synth punk / EBM
items._cn_summary: Virgin Birth 是一支来自美国肯塔基州路易斯维尔的工业朋克三人组，新作《The Dead End》收录六首歌曲，于2026年10月由独立厂牌 Never Nervous Records 发行。乐队由主唱兼合成器手 Phillip Olympia、吉他手 Jake Miller 和贝斯手 Matt Haas 组成，录音在路易斯维尔本地的 The Slaughtered Lamb Studio 完成。厂牌在介绍中将这张 EP 定位为乐队对电子音乐、朋克以及当代荒诞现实的回应，与早期作品中宏观视角的崩塌叙事相比，新作更趋内向、压迫与私密。乐队此前的作品包括2023年的首张 EP《The Forest》、2024年的《From Behind》以及2025年的全长专辑《Total Annihilation》，均通过同一厂牌发行，录音工作也始终由 Miller 在同一录音室完成。文章以新闻通稿形式呈现，缺乏对音乐具体声响、编配或创作手法的深入评论。

items._cn_summary: 这张作品以世纪双星100周年为契机，对爵士史两大经典进行当代重构。制作人将原作骨架拆解后，注入了浩室律动、放克质感、雷鬼律动、拉丁节奏与非洲音乐元素，形成跨地域的混合声场。'All Blues'的演绎呈现出强烈的律动推进感，'Resolution'则以紧绷的氛围张力重塑原作的精神维度。评论认为作品并非简单复刻经典，而是带着明确的当代立场重新解读——通过这张再创作返回原作时，听感经验也随之被刷新。整体制作在致敬与重构之间找到了平衡点，既保留原作骨架又注入新血肉。

items._cn_summary: Modulisme 第 146 期聚焦法国电子音乐人 Poborsk（本名 Patrice Curtillat）的模块化合成器创作。该项目有意偏离精致的电子结构构建，转而拥抱声音的不稳定性：节奏持续偏移，微小的机械性动作不断生成，音色之间发生碰撞，系统被允许以不可预测的方式自行运作。创作脉络从早期的卡式磁带多轨录音与吉他逐步延伸至当前的模块化实践。这一期的核心价值在于呈现模块合成器作为"失控工具"的美学可能——艺术家并非追求控制每一个参数，而是让系统自身的偏差与故障成为创作的素材来源，对偏好实验声响与即兴电子的受众具有参考意义。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Entropia' is the debut studio album by Swedish progressive metal act Pain of Salvation, originallyreleased by Avalon in Japan and later reissued by Inside Out, which would become the band's primarylabel for decades to come. Fronted by eccentric multi-instrumentalist Daniel Gildenl�w, the band wasformed in 1984 under the name Reality, gradually evolving into the excellent project we recognizetoday as PoS. As for the album 'Entropia' itself, it had been in the works for quite some time priorto its release. And while most debut albums tend to be uneven and unpredictable, I find thisparticular one to be a surprisingly well-executed amalgamation of styles and influences that allowsthe band's own identity to shine through as well. Primarily a progressive metal album, 'Entropia'seems to draw as much from Faith No More and Mike Patton as it does from bands like Dream Theaterand Fates Warning, with which it shares some similarities. There is a claustrophobic, dark, andalmost urban atmosphere on this record, which to me is in line with what other prog metal acts hadbeen exploring stylistically around that time.The music on 'Entropia' is nevertheless difficult to describe, as it ranges from melodic andstraightforward progressive rock, to chaotic, technical, and rhythmically dynamic heavy prog. Highlyeclectic, this album occasionally feels overstimulating and difficult to follow, which is somethingthe band would remedy on future releases. On top of that, the concept behind 'Entropia' is quitecomplicated, too, and the band does not make it easy to decipher either. So try not to dig too muchinto the lyrics or the meaning behind each track but rather enjoy the dense rollercoaster of stylesand moods that this collection represents. For me 'Entropia' carries several characteristic elementsof the classic Pain of Salvation sound, but they are underdeveloped on this debut LP. Of course,attentive listeners will find plenty of curious elements and motifs scattered throughout the record,and in particular on stronger tracks like '! (Foreword)', 'Winning a War', 'People Passing By', 'Tothe End', and 'Nightmist'. And while this is not a favorite Pain of Salvation album of mine, I mustadmit that as a document of the progressive metal scene of the late 90s it is impressive andpromising.
items._genre: progressive metal / eclectic / experimental rock
items._cn_summary: 这是瑞典前卫金属乐队Pain of Salvation的处女作专辑，融合了Faith No More式的实验气质与Dream Theater式的技术金属框架。整张作品在风格上跨度极大，从旋律化的前卫摇滚到混乱、技术化的重型段落均有涵盖，音乐呈现出一种幽闭、黑暗、近乎都市化的氛围。专辑概念围绕熵展开，歌词与主题都相当晦涩复杂，乐队并未刻意降低理解门槛。评论者认为这张作品虽然偶有过度刺激、难以跟进的段落，但作为一支乐队的首张专辑，其风格融合的成熟度与对自身声音的辨识度已相当可观。亮点曲目包括开场段、战争主题与夜雾等多首。总体而言，这是一张在九十年代末前卫金属场景中展现潜力与实验精神的处女作，但评论者也坦言这并非其个人最偏爱的PoS专辑。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — This is from my blog "Scott's Song by Song Spotlights" with links for listening and purchasing.Clicked 5, but really a 4.5...4 is too low!T.A.P are a progressive rock band led by composer/keyboardist Michael Jobborn. On their first album, which I have not heard (2023's "Paradigms") the band was rounded out by Warr-guitarist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Cook (Phase of Twilight and others) and Guitarist/Vocalist/multi-instrumentalist Suzi James (Fearful Symmetry, whose wonderful latest album "I've Started?So I'll Finish" is reviewed on this blog as well!). Paul Sears and Bill Bachman were both contributors on the first album on the drum throne. This time around Bill Bachman is a full member. Bill is renowned for his work as a drumming educator, including his work with several Drum Corps around the US. (DCI- Drum Corps International- is a deep rabbit hole that I have been familiar with since my college days!) But his prog resume is impressive as well: (From the press release) "Bill is the drummer for Herd of Instinct, Spoke of Shadows, has toured with progressive rock artist Neal Morse, is on recordings with Trey Gunn (King Crimson), Colin Edwin (Porcupine Tree), Adam Holzman (Miles Davis & Steven Wilson), and Gerald Albright (Grammy award winning saxophonist)". So, the musical talent in this band is absolutely staggering!This album comes courtesy of Anne-Claire Rallo of Bad Dog Promotions. As always, I receive no additional compensation and am free to "call it like I hear it". In fact, when I received the email offering this review to me from Anne-Claire, I replied, "You had me at Suzi James". The album "Paradigms II" is to be released on October 3, 2026, on the Prog Rock Essentials label (Ordering info follows the review). As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Time to dig into the music!T.A.P are:Michael Jobborn - concepts, keysMark Cook - Warr guitar, bass, 12-string guitar, synth, sitar, strings, choirSuzi James - acoustic/electric guitars, keys, flute, violinBill Bachman - drums, percussionAdditional Contributors on tracks:2. Chris Gill - guitarChris Messina - synth4. Steve Bonino - guitar, lyrics/vocals5. Gayle Ellett - mellotron, acoustic/electric guitars6. Massimo Pieretti - piano, synthGayle Ellett - bouzouki, mellotron8. Tenk van Dool - mandolin, guitarChris Gill - guitarTrack 1 - Galaxy Unknown (4:28)An organ riff, accented with drums starts us off with an odd meter. The rest of the band soon joins in. There is a guitar solo after around 45 seconds. A softer section follows with alternating acoustic and electric instruments in the spotlight. This is a wonderful instrumental musical journey with many layers. As one might expect, the talent level here is through the roof! A terrific opener!Track 2 - A Beacon of Light (12:17)This one fades in with some guitar effects and synth tones. It feels like the first rays of sunlight at dawn, matching the title. Electric piano chords bring a sense of rhythm. The bass line provides melodic movement. The chords are layered among many instruments, giving a rich tonal palate. This is moving at a moderately slow tempo and a relaxed feel. The guitar solo that happens at around the 4-minute mark brings a balance of melodicism and complexity. A droning section after that leads to an upbeat groove on the bass and drums. It begins to take on a jazz fusion flavor. Synth and guitar solos float over the top of the rhythm bed. Just before 7:30 things calm down and a new section begins. Sitar sounds are a part of the soundscape. Bill's marching band experience shows in his snare part. At 8:45 we are down to lead guitar, bass and keys. The drums subtly return. We are in a slower 6-8 at this point. At 9:55 a more strident beat that reminds me of old TV themes takes over. There are so many moods in this piece; I love it! At 11:30, it reminds me of how it began. What an absolutely fantastic instrumental piece of music!Track 3 - A Dramatic Interlude (4:06)Electric piano, bass and lead guitar start this off. The drums enter a moment later. This is in a moderately slow 6-8, so far, but the title tells me something is going to happen. The tempo increases slightly and becomes more rhythmic after a small crescendo. I believe that is the Warr guitar taking the solo that follows. I love the staccato bass and guitar riff at around 2:20. Things begin to build up at around 3:20. The track ends with a long, sustained chord. A wonderful piece, but not as dramatic as the title indicated. Track 4 - A Hole in the Ground (6:14)Rich electric piano chords and clean guitars start us off here. Lead guitar emerges. And then--Vocals! Guest musician Steve Bonino is on this track with guitars and vocals. (This is not the first time his name has appeared in one of my reviews!) The drums begin to emerge as we progress. Mark Cook's basslines are fantastic on this album. Steve's voice seems a little buried in the mix at times. The drums might be a little too far back at times, as well. I like the song, but I don't feel like it's mixed as well as it could be. It would benefit from a better presentation. It ends with droning sounds.Track 5 - 4th Dimensional Wave (11:50)Sound effects fade in and guitars join. This starts out sounding like some sort of alarm. Soon, though, the music gets melodic with a fantastic guitar solo; I believe it is Suzi James. We are in a moderately slow tempo. The keys are playing a mellotron style chorus behind the solo. Some intricate rhythmic patterns follow. This keeps building, slowly and gradually. At around 4:20 we get into odd meters. At 5:45, the rhythm shifts into a different groove. I am really enjoying this one! There are tons of changes! Gayle Ellet of Djam Karet and his band the Electromags adds his keyboard abilities to the soundscapes. Probably my favorite track, so far.Track 6 - Lyrical Paradox (3:50)This one has a bit of a swing to it. Sort of a mellow melodic tune. The sound gets bigger just after the one-minute mark. Great melodies in this one. I love the slide guitar in it; it reminds me of the slide guitar in "And You and I" from Yes. This is a nice little piece. Ellet is back with bouzouki on this, and Massimo Pieretti (whom I have reviewed as well) adds keyboards.Track 7 - Outlooks of the Closed-Minded (6:29)This opens with some accents and jazz chords. It has a fusion feel to my ears. I love the syncopated rhythms. It reminds me of the Dixie Dregs a bit. Lots of melodies wind their way through this one. Wonderful track!Track 8 - Wishful Solitude (:)This one is more up-tempo, yet lighthearted. As with most of the album, the melodies are abundant! At around 3:15 Suzi plays her flute. There are many interesting things in the soundscape. At just be for the 5-minute mark, a descending synth part that sounds like the 70s idea of a UFO landing takes over, then we get a bit funky! At around 6:45 we get a psychedelic organ sound. This is a very cool piece with many different things going on. Tenk van Dool (who I am not familiar with) plays the mandolin at around 8:45. The melodies intertwine as we approach the ending. This is a wonderfully arranged prog instrumental. Great way to end this wonderful album.OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:I really liked that a lot! Unfortunately, I am not sure what happened on track 4, "A Hole in the Ground". I have always liked Steve Bonino's contributions, and he always seems to be a good guy in the online interactions I have had with him, but something just didn't work for me on that track. Otherwise, this is a fantastic album of mainly instrumental prog with some fusion tendencies. I give this a 4.5 out of 5 or 90%. Recommended!
items._genre: eclectic progressive rock / symphonic prog / instrumental prog
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以器乐演奏为核心的前卫摇滚专辑，由键盘手Michael Jobborn领衔，集合了Warr吉他手Mark Cook、吉他手Suzi James以及鼓手Bill Bachman等多位资深乐手。乐队编制横跨键盘、多种吉他、弦乐、笛与打击乐，乐手履历涉及Trey Gunn、Colin Edwin、Porcupine Tree等前卫圈名字，演奏水准扎实。曲目结构呈现典型的前卫摇滚模式：开篇曲《Galaxy Unknown》以管风琴riff与复合节拍起手，叠加吉他独奏与原声段落；《A Beacon of Light》长达十二分钟，以吉他效果与合成器铺陈氛围，段落之间缓慢过渡。整体呈现偏向学院化、技术化的器乐叙事路线，在小厂牌Prog Rock Essentials发行，融合度与乐手多样性为其加分，但创新性表达与传统前卫摇滚语法仍有一定距离。

items.body: Turn it off, this channel’s boring, see? This is not how my life was supposed to be So I take this poison inside of me There is a delicious stupidity in trying to escape a miserable situation by making choices almost guaranteed to leave you worse off. The promise of feeling alive again has filled bars, emptied bank accounts, inspired regrettable phone calls, and sent countless people back into relationships they had good reason to leave. New England darkwave outfit Ghost Painted Sky have built Kissing Lions around one of humanity’s more dependable talents: recognizing the jaws directly in front of us and deciding, against every scrap of available evidence, to lean closer anyway. Taken from the forthcoming Failure Blooms, the song captures those moments when boredom and disappointment have accumulated enough weight that almost any escape starts to look reasonable, including the varieties with sharp teeth. The band began in Massachusetts in 2014 as David Strong’s project, expanding into a genuine partnership when vocalist and lyricist Lisa Wood joined in 2018. Guitarist Michael Boudreau followed in 2022, while longtime collaborator Aurora Grabill adds violin here and elsewhere on the album. What they produce on “Kissing Lions” belongs comfortably within darkwave and post-punk, though its real engine is psychological: the familiar urge to make some reckless little bargain with yourself because ordinary life has become intolerably beige. Wood sings from inside that bargain. The rising tide gets pushed away, the television gets switched off, poison gets swallowed, and eventually the lion receives a kiss directly on the mouth. You can practically hear the terrible idea becoming attractive in real time. The metaphor works because lions remain perfectly innocent in this arrangement. They were always going to bite. The speaker is the one grabbing the teeth. “Kissing Lions describes those mostly vain attempts to seize on anything that creates a fleeting feeling of being alive for a moment amid relentless waves of the humdrum, doldrums, and failure, which so often end up being misguided and ultimately just creating a thicker mire even more strangling than the original situation one sought to escape… bad decisions that bite back and create further downward spirals,” says Strong. Strong’s accompanying video stretches that idea across generations, combining 8mm footage shot by his grandfather, Herbert Virta, with material from a 2023 virtual performance for Goths for Sanctuaries and footage from The Heavy Culture Cooperative in Easthampton, Massachusetts, filmed in August 2026 with projected visuals by Daisy. Past and present collide without becoming sentimental window dressing; time simply keeps advancing while people continue finding increasingly elaborate ways to get bitten. Watch the video for Kissing Lions below: The digital maxi-single adds the brighter Kissing Lions (Effervescent Remix) and My Words Are Not My Own, which turns toward conformity and the slow surrender of individual voice. Mixed and mastered by William Faith, Failure Blooms follows 2018’s Flightless. Eight years later, Ghost Painted Sky sounds preoccupied with failure less as an ending than as a remarkably fertile place to keep making the same disastrous choices. Listen to Kissing Lions below and order the single here. items._genre: darkwave / post-punk / goth
items._cn_summary: 新英格兰暗潮三人组 Ghost Painted Sky 的单曲《Kissing Lions》以"明知是陷阱却仍主动靠近"为核心隐喻，歌词刻画了人在麻木与失望中做出看似解脱实则更糟的选择。乐队编制在标准暗潮配置上加入小提琴，编曲并未走向极端实验，但在心理叙事的驱动下展现出明确的情绪弧线——电视被关掉、毒药被吞下、狮子被亲吻，隐喻的推进清晰且具有文学质感。歌曲所属专辑 Failure Blooms 即将发行，附赠曲目包含更明亮的混音版本以及一首转向探讨从众主题的作品。MV 将祖父 8mm 影像、虚拟演出与现场实录并置，让时间感成为另一层叙事载体。整体而言，这是一支在类型范围内认真打磨歌词与概念的作品，具备暗潮应有的冷峻气质，但声音层面的冒险性有限。

items.body: I had hoped to be seen by you Unbroken gaze like a sweet arrow Could you ever feel my eyes on you Bathing you in my desire Desire has a way of making the body speak before the mind has decided what to say: flushed cheeks, an aching chest, the unreasonable hope that somebody might feel a glance from across the room. In the video for Sacred Hearts, Gloria de Oliveira takes those private sensations onto the streets of Hamburg’s St. Pauli district, where barroom lamps, photo-booth portraits, and the company of women give longing somewhere to live. The song’s burning heart finds a fitting companion in the red lights overhead, while affection passes between its subjects through looks, laughter, and the small pleasure of being together. The Berlin-based German-Brazilian musician and visual artist shares the video for the third single from her forthcoming album The Lying Swans, due October 30, 2026, through La Double Vie and Cargo Records. Produced by Randall Dunn, whose work includes records with Anna von Hausswolff and Marissa Nadler, Sacred Hearts considers the exhilaration and anxiety of giving yourself over to another person, particularly when the body seems to have made that decision ahead of you. The opening guitar figures carry an almost medieval character, joined by bright, percussive tones with the delicacy of a hammered dulcimer. Matt Chamberlain’s drumming briefly suggests the forward motion of Kate Bush’s Running Up That Hill before settling into the song’s own gait. Deep resonant strings lend the arrangement weight, while synthesizers soften its edges and extend its peculiar, old-world atmosphere. The tones and melody evoke a folk ballad like Nick Cave’s The Weeping Song, with the spaciousness of a Western just beyond the song’s antique ornamentation. De Oliveira sings into that space with a delicate quiver that evokes Elizabeth Fraser, with a classical poise softened by the intimacy of her delivery. Lennard Zander’s acoustic, electric, and 12-string guitars trace fine melodic lines without disturbing the vocal’s tenderness; Arjan Miranda anchors the arrangement on bass, while de Oliveira, Dunn, and Úlfur Hansson add layers of synthesizer. The music leaves her exposed yet almost weightless, as if every declaration of love might tip her toward losing her footing. The lyrics measure desire through its physical symptoms, moving from fever and sleeplessness toward the hope contained in a hand’s touch. To be seen becomes as urgent as to be loved, and the repeated attempts to contain that feeling only reveal its scale. Yet, the song’s title draws on an image de Oliveira has carried since childhood, joining religious devotion to the unruly sensations of romantic attachment. “The Catholic image of Christ’s Sacred Heart – a heart literally engulfed in flames – has struck me since childhood.” “Of course it’s meant to symbolise God’s boundless and passionate love for mankind – however, as John Keats once wrote, ‘I am certain of nothing but of the holiness of the heart’s affections, and the truth of imagination’. And how does it feel to give yourself over to that affection and desire despite fear? With this song, I wanted to capture these seemingly contrasting sentiments.” Shot and directed by award-winning Turkish filmmaker Seda Kaçak, and edited by de Oliveira, the video stars London actress Mona Najma alongside Eva Rogalla. Kaçak follows the women through St. Pauli in handheld close-ups, catching them sharing drinks, posing for photo-booth pictures, and moving between daylight streets and richly coloured interiors. Superimposed faces and starbursts around the lights give these ordinary pleasures an enchanted quality. Conceived as a homage to the bond between women, the film offers an affectionate counterpoint to the song’s solitary ache: companionship makes room for feelings that can otherwise become overwhelming. Watch the video for Sacred Hearts below: A classically trained singer whose acting work includes Babylon Berlin and Christian Petzold’s Undine, de Oliveira released music with the darkwave and synthpop duo lovespells before her 2020 debut album Fascination. Her 2022 collaboration with David Lynch’s longtime sound designer Dean Hurley, Oceans of Time, followed through Sacred Bones. Across those releases, she has explored dream pop, ethereal wave, ambient music, and the influence of her Brazilian roots, alongside work for theatre, film, and London Fashion Week. Recorded in Iceland, New York, and Berlin, The Lying Swans extends those interests across nine songs concerned with trauma, perception, and the difficult return of trust. Its title invokes the myth of Leda, while its literary references include John Keats, Emily Brontë, Anne Sexton, and Milton’s Paradise Lost. Within that broader examination of love and illusion, Sacred Hearts holds open the possibility of affection despite fear. Listen to Sacred Hearts below or via streaming services, and pre-order The Lying Swans here. The album is out October 30, 2026, on digital, vinyl, CD, and cassette. items.body: …O sun, that healest all distempered vision, thou dost content me so, when thou resolvest,that doubting pleases me no less than knowing! -Dante Alighieri, Divine Comedy Golden Apes have spent more than twenty years making music for people who think a bass guitar should sound slightly dangerous, a baritone ought to carry bad news with dignity, and every decent chorus deserves at least one guitar line large enough to knock over the furniture. On The Sun Came Up Tremendously, the Berlin band sounds completely at home with that assignment. Ten songs move between post-punk, dark wave, gothic rock, dreampop, and bruised alternative rock, yet the record never feels like a display cabinet of influences. Golden Apes know this country too well for tourism. They have lived here. There is plenty of history in these songs, of course. You can hear The Cure in the open space around certain guitar lines, Chameleons in the upward sweep of others, Cocteau Twins in the gauzier passages, and the severe romantic machinery of Clan of Xymox when the keyboards begin closing in. White Lies, Interpol, Lowlife, and The Horrors, drift through the bloodline. Yet Golden Apes have reached the point where influence is less a matter of borrowing than instinct. Twenty-plus years will do that to a band. Eventually your record collection gets absorbed into your nervous system. The Sun Came Up Tremendously follows 2024’s Our Ashes at the End of the Day as the second installment in a planned trilogy, with material written across 2024 and 2025 and recorded at Thommy Hein Studios in Berlin between late 2025 and early 2026. Thommy Hein also contributes guitar, joining vocalist and keyboardist Peer Lebrecht, guitarists Maximilian Hennig and Stephan Schoenfeld, bassist Christian Lebrecht, and drummer Salomon Bosse. The production favors size without polishing away the pressure inside these songs. Basslines keep pushing forward, drums give the record a stern physical gait, and the guitars are allowed to bloom, bruise, and occasionally swallow the room. Farewell begins with a plaintive guitar that sounds as if it’s emerging from a dream, and an open space that immediately calls The Chameleons to mind, though The Horrors’ later grandeur also shows in the way the arrangement keeps adding height. It is a lovely opening, sad without collapsing into self-pity, and expansive without turning into marble-statue rock. Peer Lebrecht sings as though he has already accepted whatever the song is grieving, which somehow makes the ache sharper. By the time the rhythm section settles in, the track feels less like a goodbye than the long walk away from one. The Light (Inside Us) comes on harder. The guitars widen, Christian Lebrecht’s bass digs in, and the verses carry a conversational quality before the chorus breaks open into a shoegaze-heavy rush. The seduction of scale takes center stage: the chorus is huge enough to make a ceiling seem temporarily optional, yet the band keeps enough dirt in the guitars to prevent grandeur from becoming ceremony. This is music reaching for the upper rows while keeping both boots on the club floor. Milk and Poison turns inward and drops the temperature. Its opening feels like ripples on water with dream-pop textures, though the song soon settles into an anthemic ballad buoyed by these currents, sailing on broad synth pads, acoustic accents, surging guitars, and Peer’s low, expressive voice. He has one of those voices that can make a grocery list sound vaguely incriminating, and Golden Apes wisely avoid burying it beneath unnecessary decoration. The arrangement gives him room, then closes around him in slow degrees. Resistance is where the record’s architecture comes into sharpest focus. A resonant guitar figure opens the track, answered by a low keyboard tone, as hi-hats hiss at the edges and the bass builds steady pressure. The arrangement grows heavier until the guitars reach the emotional scale of mid-eighties gothic rock. Peer remains composed as the band swells around him, and that restraint gives the song its authority. Near the center, a clean, melodic guitar solo arrives with almost startling simplicity, offering a brief clearing before the vocal returns with greater weight. No pyrotechnics are needed; the song already knows where its gravity lies. At intervals, the drums break into splashes and the rhythm pulls back, leaving more air around Peer’s euphoric delivery. The measured bass, sober guitar tone, and baritone gravity recall Scottish cult band Lowlife, while the surrounding textures remain recognizably Golden Apes. Helion heads toward the same terrain as Clan of Xymox and The Chameleons, with traces of Joy Division in its resigned vocals and the stern drive of its rhythm section. An emotional barrage of drums and surging guitars carries the song forward, giving its sense of exhaustion an almost overwhelming physical force. There is something perversely satisfying about how controlled it remains amid all that turbulence. Plenty of bands mistake gloom for permission to wallow; Golden Apes keep pushing through it. It is the sort of song you want to hear live, feel in your chest, and carry with you on the walk home after everybody else has disappeared. Where the River Ran slows the pace and brings Peer’s baritone into Nick Cave territory. The drums begin with a plodding military tattoo, giving the song a processional character, while guitar and synth gradually stretch outward until the arrangement takes on a shoegaze breadth. The transition works because the band allows it to happen patiently. What begins in discipline ends in something far less contained. Evelyn (One Day) opens with a long sigh, which is about as efficient a piece of scene-setting as anybody could ask for. The resemblance to Lowlife grows even stronger here, recalling the Scottish band at their most wistful, thoughtful, and romantic. Dream-pop synth textures surround Peer’s voice, while dramatic splashes of guitar and percussion accent the song’s tender emotion, not unlike The Cure’s “Push.” Once again, Golden Apes take the form of a ballad and keep expanding it until the walls seem to move outward. The song swells like the ocean, its quieter passages gathering strength before euphoric surges of guitar and drums break across the arrangement. Their fondness for large choruses could become ridiculous in less experienced hands, but the rhythm section keeps the drama tethered to muscle. Radiation opens with a steady drumbeat and dirgeful tones before Peer’s rich, deep baritone bellows with unusual force, almost thunderous without losing definition. The chiming guitars and rhythm section pull back to give him room, though the melodic bassline remains palpable, felt in the heart and bones. With the song’s titular refrain, a surge of guitars seems to radiate toward the fingertips, giving its emotional release a physical reach. The drums then quicken in anticipation, and the guitars sweep in sustained arcs before the refrain returns, each repetition gathering strength from the space the band leaves around the voice. City Walls slows everything again, returning to the Cave-like gravity heard earlier. The drums drag with deliberate weight while a manic hi-hat keeps scratching at the surface, and eerie female backing vocals add an uneasy human presence around Peer’s lead. The song feels boxed in by design. Space exists, but none of it seems comfortable. Every instrument appears to occupy its own corner while the room keeps shrinking. Then comes Dreams (Gone By), opening with strange industrial textures before a weighty rhythm section and eerie synth tones take control, recalling London After Midnight’s Kiss. The percussion has real physical heft, but the gloom gradually recedes as the song opens into the brighter dream-pop romance of Modern English and Lowlife. Golden Apes carry that change with the emotional swell established throughout the album, letting the arrangement expand without losing the force of its darker beginnings. A brief pause for a wistful guitar chime offers some breathing room before the gothic dance rhythm returns, subtly brighter now, and the song surges again. As a closer, it gives the album one last change in texture, moving from industrial unease toward romantic release while retaining the emotional weight of the previous nine tracks. By this point, the record has passed through goth, post-punk, dreampop, dark wave, and broad alternative rock without sounding indecisive. Golden Apes can write a severe club track, a huge guitar chorus, a graveyard ballad, or a slow piece that sounds built for stained glass and bad decisions, and somehow Peer Lebrecht’s voice keeps the record unified. His baritone carries longing, isolation, regret, and the occasional flash of release without turning every lyric into a public execution. There is drama here, plenty of it, but the band understands proportion. Even at their biggest, they leave enough space for the songs to breathe. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is also the work of a band with very little interest in pretending they discovered any of these styles yesterday. Golden Apes’ long touring history, including appearances at Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Castle Party, and Murder of Crows, plus stages shared with The Chameleons, Pink Turns Blue, And Also the Trees, She Past Away, Whispering Sons, TRAITRS, Then Comes Silence, and others, has given them the practical education that comes from watching songs survive outside the studio. The title may promise sunrise, though nobody should expect birds chirping outside a kitchen window. Golden Apes prefer their light complicated, filtered through regret, desire, bad choices, and the stubborn suspicion that survival can occasionally be worth the inconvenience of a journey through hell and back. The only way to reach dawn, after all, is through the night. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is out now through Icy Cold Records. Listen to the album below and order here. items._cn_summary: Golden Apes这支柏林后朋克乐队在成立二十余年后推出三曲 trilogy 的第二章《The Sun Came Up Tremendously》。专辑在制作上强调规模感与压迫感的平衡，贝斯线持续推进、鼓点沉稳有力，吉他声部时而绽放时而粗粝，键盘在必要时收紧空间。乐评指出乐队对The Cure、Chameleons、Cocteau Twins、Clan of Xymox等前辈的吸收已内化为本能，而非简单模仿。开篇曲《Farewell》以梦境般的吉他引入，悲怆而不自溺；中段作品如《The Light (Inside Us)》转向更厚重的shoegaze化处理，合唱段落尺度夸张。整体而言，这是一张风格扎实、情感克制的暗黑系后朋克作品，乐队以稳定的成熟度延续传统，但在实验性和跨界融合层面突破有限。

items.body: Label: Out Of Your Head Records, 2026 Personnel - David Léon: saxophone, flute; Kenny Warren: trumpet; Stephan Crump: bass; Ches Smith: drums. Bassist and composer Stephan Crump, a musician of extraordinary passion and lyricism, put together a crisp, bright new ensemble for his latest outing, Passerine , a work of originals inspired by the various nesting techniques of birds. Relying on a frontline composed of Cuban-American saxophonist and flutist David Léon and trumpeter Kenny Warren, and pairing up beautifully with the resourceful drummer Ches Smith, Crump has something fresh to say. " Stuck " firstly evolves in a 3/4 time signature, displaying a big, round bass sound that shelters sharp unison melody. Léon narrates a story over an arco bass ostinato, while Smith explores toms and cymbal sounds with sagacity. There's a change of pace and texture for Warren's expressive solo, and the interplay between the rhythm team becomes more defiant, leading to a swinging passage before returning to the initial waltzing breeze. " Glide " is executed with a compelling rhythmic quality underneath—Crump incorporating effortless bass pedals, pizzicato routes, and cool grooves that find consistent support in Smith's nicely brushed skins. On flute, Léon stands out, drawing from melodic and harmonic minor modes in his improvisation. " Weavers " and " Twenty-Five " are warm meditative exercises where all members leave flowery scents in the air while rowing in the same direction. The former piece rests on a relaxed bass harmonic conduction that breathes at a challenging tempo, having charismatic, pure-toned unisons running atop. The latter is a shape-shifter that initiates with a sparse bass figure, understated drumming, a pellucid flute whose gentle dance emulates the chirp of birds, and introspective trumpet. Warren and Léon always take maximum advantage of their instruments to create dual melodic lines that feel luminous and often varied in shape. That's the case on " Fly ", a well-balanced 3/4 canvas painted with a certain wry melancholia. Breathable bass and brush work create space and smooth out the environment, culminating in a pulsating bass pedal point at the center of the outro vamp. With sensitive collaborative input from the musicians enlisted, Passerine is a point of departure and an embrace of transformation for Crump. It's also detailed with rigor without abandoning the freedom of creating spontaneously. The composer's sophisticated sound and gracious storytelling are filtered into the album's sequence. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Stuck ► 02 - Glide ► 03 - Weavers

items.body: “Nothing lasts, you see, not even the thoughts inside you. And you musn’t waste your time looking for them. Once a thing is gone, that is the end of it.” – Paul Auster, ‘In The Country of Last Things’. Taking inspiration from ‘In The Country of Last Things’, a 1987 novel written by Paul Auster, ‘Last Things’ seeks to isolate itself in the countryside, distancing itself from the fast pace of the urban lifestyle for something more contemplative and lonely; looking for the literal wilderness after dissatisfaction or unrest. Nature is beautiful and beneficial to one’s health and wellbeing, but it can also be vicious and unpredictable. The countryside can be relaxing and peaceful, but it can also catch someone unawares and leave them reeling, as audiences found out in The Blair Witch Project. A foreboding presence sticks to the prospect of isolation like glue; the stark, swaying branches and the yawning fields can sprout the genre of folk horror with ease, and seemingly without any additional help; it comes from their own design. This complete edition of Last Things takes up three discs and includes music recorded under his The Inventors of Aircraft moniker, further planting Phil Tomsett’s music in the soil. Described as a ‘personal struggle through hum, thunder, and dread’, Last Things is something of an audio artefact, a recently unearthed relic which, when played back, translates Auster’s prose into an earthy type of music. Last Things has lain dormant, entrenched in the damp soil, for time immemorial, long enough to ingratiate itself with the song of the land and the rustling of the fields, only slightly decaying as it ages. Contentedness and a flowering of peace may be held in one hand, but the woods can also be wild, its cabins holding a wolf in disguise of a sweet grandmother. Last Things moves from bejewelled beauty to monumental dread. In some ways, the music is like the exploration of an old house, deep in the country, where spiders have nestled and settled, and the floorboards creak with age, having not had a foot to press upon and upset its wood. Like a self-made contagion, loneliness seeps into the air, mingling with the gathering dreamcatchers of dust. Tracks such as ‘I Long For Days That Never Existed’ and ‘These Are The Last Things, She Wrote’ are indicative of the music having been through rough patches, and its moss-streaked textures seem to creep around the rooms with downcast body language, close to mourning with its lowered head as it looks to retreat back into its shell, locking and bolting the door to this great old house and never leaving, even as the growing vines slink over the windowsills and the day turns to dusk. www.wistrec.com

items._cn_summary: Phil Tomsett 与 The Inventors of Aircraft 的《Last Things》是一部受保罗·奥斯特小说启发而创作的三碟套装作品，将散文中的末日感与乡野恐怖氛围转化为声响。整张专辑呈现一种被土壤掩埋又重新出土的质感：嗡鸣、雷鸣与不安的情绪交织，音乐从装饰性的美丽滑向巨大的恐惧。评论将专辑比作对一座荒废乡间老屋的探索——木板吱呀作响，灰尘如捕梦网般聚拢，孤独像自生的传染病渗入空气。苔藓覆盖的纹理在房间里蔓延，肢体语言低垂，近乎哀悼。专辑收录了如《I Long For Days That Never Existed》与《These Are The Last Things, She Wrote》等曲目，通过自然的田野录音与暗哑的氛围层构建，既保留乡村的宁静意象，又深掘其潜藏的野性与危险。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于艺术家驻留皇家植物园的七年项目，以园中最古老的一棵棕榈树被砍伐后的故事为起点，将人声、钢琴与精心设计的声景编织成一场关于自然、历史与记忆的仪式。Karine Polwart 的演唱温暖且富有同情心，Dave Milligan 的钢琴低调而敏锐，整体呈现出内省而庄严的气质。歌曲旋律带有苏格兰民谣的根源感，同时融入跨文化视角的联想。专辑虽以简约编制为主，却在克制中展开宏大叙事，让听众从一棵树的命运中读出时间的流转与生命的延续。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: Sudan Dudan是挪威二人组，由Marit Karlberg和Anders Erik Røine组成，这张专辑是他们的第五张作品。整张专辑以原声吉他为主，辅以挪威传统乐器如fiddle、langeleik、lyre和口琴等。专辑虽以"Dark Refrains"为名，整体氛围却更多是反思性的。歌词涉及神话、谜语、自然与失落等主题，以挪威语呈现。专辑中有轻快时刻，如《Bagatelle》以法国民谣旋律为基础加入非传统和声，《Rulleball》运用挪威特有的tralling无词人声唱法。最后一曲《Skriften på veggen》罕见地加入电吉他，深沉twangy音色让人联想到Duane Eddy或David Lynch配乐。这是一张制作精良、富于想象力的民谣作品，融合了挪威传统元素与一些现代声音探索。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 专辑以历史叙事为框架，追溯十九世纪墨西哥牛仔携吉他前往夏威夷放牧的跨文化旅程，将西班牙语与夏威夷语歌曲互译，重新编配两国传统曲目，并融入新创作与美国民间音乐。十六首作品以尤克里里、墨西哥竖琴、手风琴与吉他为核心编制，在加州单室同期录音完成，保留了现场即兴与自发感。客座音乐人 Taj Mahal 与 David Hidalgo 担任催化角色，从选曲到编曲全程参与，前者在录音中示范教学段落尤为生动。专辑体现语言、年龄、性别与文化层面的合作精神，滑棒吉他独奏与拉普钢点缀其中，既呈现墨西哥与夏威夷音乐传统的丰富性，也借 Woody Guthrie《Deportee》延伸至移民议题的社会评论维度。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由丹麦三人组合 GuldGanger 推出的数字版 EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手 Mia Guldhammer 领衔。五首作品以传统音乐为主，成员各自带入不同视角参与诠释。开场曲以粗粝的节奏展示主唱嗓音的说服力，铙钹与风袋在原创作品中提供推进动力。传统曲目中扬琴铺陈细腻和声背景，口簧琴与长笛交织于终曲器乐段，形成偏离常规的聆听体验。整体散发着沉稳而古旧的氛围，五首曲目已展现出超越首作的成熟度与完成度，为后续完整专辑埋下期待。北欧传统器乐与声乐融合的世界音乐路线，偏向传统诠释而非实验性突破。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._genre: New Orleans R&B / funk / blues / Mardi Gras revue
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了Dr. John于1999年在德国莱茵河畔罗蕾莱露天剧场的现场演出，由WDR电视台的Rockpalast节目录制发行。演出以新奥尔良风格的狂欢节回顾为核心，曲目涵盖经典新奥尔良标准曲与Dr. John个人代表作。乐队阵容紧凑，包括吉他、贝斯和鼓手，展现出纯熟的放克律动与节奏互动。开场的《Iko Iko》呈现半唱半吟的街头游行参与感，《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》则带有迷幻、阴郁的巫毒仪式色彩，融合丛林打击乐、诡异滑哨与迷幻吉他独奏。演出还致敬了Duke Ellington的《I'm Gonna Go Fishin'》以及Earl King的《Big Chief》作为收尾。作为横跨新奥尔良传统的音乐人，Dr. John将funk、blues、R&B与神秘主义美学结合，现场演出兼具民俗传承与个人艺术印记。
