items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._genre: nordic folk / chamber improvisation / experimental traditional
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威乐手组成三重奏，以非传统方式重新诠释斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲。素材多源自挪威与瑞典的民间旋律，但演奏方式更接近室内乐——三位乐手在音乐中进行亲密对话般的即兴交织，呈现出舞曲表面欢快之下隐藏的暗流与神秘感。Tellef Kvifte 主要以竖笛领奏旋律，跨越挪威传统之外也运用萨克斯与风笛等非常规乐器；其子 Knut Kvifte Nesheim 作为鼓手兼作曲家，致力于模糊不同音乐流派之间的界限。编曲中旋律、纹理与打击声部层层交织，有时在发展中途突然瓦解与停滞，透露出对传统素材深层意义的探索。这种将民俗舞曲解构为现代室内即兴的做法，与学院爵士和实验音乐有交集，但整体仍根植于北欧民间传统语境中。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "For the Love of Art and the Making" is the third full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act Beyond Twilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works ofanother band). The album was released through Massacre Records in April 2006. It�s the successor to"Section X" from March 2005. There has been one lineup change since "Section X" as lead vocalistKelly Sundown Carpenter has been replaced by Swedish singer Bj�rn Jansson."For the Love of Art and the Making" is quite an interesting release as it�s basically one, 37:49minutes long composition broken down into 43 sub tracks. Stylistically it�s a continuation of thepower/progressive metal style of the preceding releases and as Jansson is a suitable and not toodifferent sounding replacement for Carpenter, the change on the lead vocalist spot doesn�t changemuch in terms of consistency of the band�s sound. The many short sub tracks makes "For the Love ofArt and the Making" a very different listening experience though as the tracks form only short partsof a longer track, they don�t have much time to evolve.It�s not that this is simple or one-dimensional music, because the tracks often shift in dynamicsbetween a heavy power/progressive metal oriented approach and more subtle and mellow parts. A normalverse/chorus structured composition wouldn�t work that way because it�s longer and you have time todevelop ideas over the course of a longer playing time. Here the short track lengths mean that ideasare executed fast and they flow by even faster. I�m not sure I think it always work that well,because sometimes I feel Beyond Twilight could have done a lot more with some of the parts, but atthat point they have usually already moved on to the next section. So, although "For the Love of Art and the Making" is a both well produced and well performedrelease, the songwriting approach will probably divide the waters. There�s arguably a lot of qualityhere but as an album I�m not sure I think "For the Love of Art and the Making" works that well. Tomy ears it�s more a study in interesting ideas and high level musicianship. Thinking of "For theLove of Art and the Making" as a single coherent composition doesn�t cross my mind while listeningto the album. The song is constantly disrupted and changes gears and dynamics and it�s actually abit stressful to listen to. When that is said "For the Love of Art and the Making" is still a highquality release, but I�m pretty sure it�s an acquired taste, so enter at your own risk. A 3.5 star(70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items.body: Review by Andis — Here's a record that deserves a lot more love. We Never Lost Control is one of those albums Igenuinely enjoy, and every spin leaves me in a better mood than before. After all, what's the pointof music if it doesn't entertain you and put a smile on your face?This album will never be mentioned in the same breath as the undisputed giants of progressive rock,but that hardly matters. It's a record I keep coming back to, and one I enjoy tremendously. Germanoddballs Nine Days Wonder, a band that seemed determined to reinvent themselves with every release,followed up their wonderfully bizarre debut by making a complete stylistic U-turn. The result is analbum that's surprisingly difficult to pin down.If I had to try, I'd place it somewhere between David Bowie and Van der Graaf Generator, with atouch of Genesis and Nektar sprinkled on top. What they play could broadly be called progressiverock, but that's only part of the story. There's glam rock swagger, flashes of krautrock, bursts ofhard rock, hints of jazz rock, and all of it fronted by a wonderfully (!) theatrical vocalist. Inother words, this album stubbornly refuses to sit in a single genre box.The band's greatest strength is its energy. Driven by swirling organs and keyboards, backed by aheavy and aggressive bass, they charge through inventive progressive rock that somehow manages tocombine the punch of hard rock with the structure of prog and the occasional hook of melodic pop-rock. Had I not known they were German, I would have guessed they were British without hesitation.Side A is a thoroughly enjoyable affair, filled with melodic songs that contain just enoughprogressive trickery to keep things interesting. But it's on Side B that the real fun begins. Herethe band completely lets loose, delivering colorful, adventurous prog rock with the magnificentnine-minute epic "We Grasp the Naked Meat" as the undisputed centerpiece.We Never Lost Control is a lovable little gem of an album: quirky, energetic, unpretentious, andendlessly entertaining. Think of it as a bag of mixed candy for progressive rock fans. Maybe itisn't a masterpiece, but it's the sort of record that reminds you why digging through the lesser-known corners of the genre can be so rewarding.

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — First it was FAIRPORT CONVENTION, but STEELEYE SPAN really planted the flag, and so were followed by worthy extenders in other lands, such as MALICORNE and TRI YANN in France, ANGELO BRANDUARDI and GIAN CASTELLO in Italy, CLANNAD and HORSLIPS in Ireland, MABSANT and PERERIN in Wales, CAPERCAILLIE and RUNRIG in Scotland, OUGENWEIDE and GALAHAD in Germany, MILLADOIRO and SANGRE DE MUERDAGO in Spain, and on and on. Most played a mix of trad/arranged and original/arranged trad style, such that, if you didn't already know, you'd be challenged to distinguish one from the other. They translated ancient poetry and prose into their native language and took liberties with the original melodies when they were known at all. I count myself among those who didn't realize that at least one Finnish group belongs in such select company, but given the breadth of Finnish prog folk, which is like THIS wide, I can't say I'm surprised by the presence or the quality of TARUJEN SAARI ("the island of sagas"), right from this debut.Led by the spirited and technically irreproachable vocals and woodwinds of Kaisa Saari, the hurdy gurdy and sundry from veteran TAPIO MATTLAR, twin violins, and a host of other folk instrumentation, this opening shot straddles all the aforementioned genealogical lines and draws a few of their own. When they choose a tune already well known to the type of people who would listen to this album in the first place, like "The Blacksmith", they give it a fresh spin, in this case it's more potent than the diva-ish LOREENA MCKENNITT rendition or the dirge like versions by STEELEYE SPAN when they were still finding themselves. They even tap the Swedes for the insistent "Margareeta". But the obvious standout here is Sinun Siniset silmasi" (your blue eyes), which merges flawless vocals, organic melody and guest cello.It's worth mentioning that for 30+ years a world beat group named VAARTINA has decorated their own room in trad oriented Finnish folk to an appreciative audience, but TARUJEN SAARI in unison pushes against the 4 (or however many) walls and thus, if not on the island of which they sing, can at least see it from their terrasse.
items._genre: prog folk / folk rock / nordic folk
items._cn_summary: 这张芬兰前卫民谣专辑以丰富的器乐编制为核心，包含手摇风琴、双小提琴、木管及大提琴等传统乐器。由Kaisa Saari主导的人声与木管表现活泼且技术无可挑剔，Hurdy-gurdy则由老兵Tapio Mattlar操持。乐队在改编传统曲目时进行了大胆的再创作，例如对经典曲目的诠释超越了Loreena McKennitt的版本，也优于Steeleye Span早期沉重的处理方式。原创曲目融合了完美的人声、有机的旋律与客座大提琴，展现出芬兰民谣的独特气质。作为芬兰本土的prog folk作品，它与英国、法国、爱尔兰、威尔士等地的民谣复兴运动一脉相承，将传统诗歌与散文以母语重新诠释，并在旋律处理上展现出独立的艺术视角。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — A crisp, violin and guitar led prog act can't help but invoke a certain era of a certain UK prog monarch led by ROBERT FRIPP, and this instrumental album isn't unworthy of such a parallel, but this is mostly in the distorted icy leads and the jazz inflections. With no vocals and a tendency to prefer structured jamming over improv, not to mention a folk orientation that Crimson increasingly set aside after 1972, it would be as unfair to SCARLET THREAD as it is to an obvious mentor to stretch this analogy any further. A better comparison might be Montreal's TALISMA or, originating in the HACKETT school, MR GIL/BELIEVE or HARNAKIS. Among fellow Finns, perhaps AQUAPLAN but without vocals, at least for now.As I said, this is jamming but in a disciplined and repetitive way that generally works well enough and is nothing if not appealing to prog ears, though everything seems a bit interchangeable - throw in a guitar motif, enhance with violin, maybe add flute, then move on to another violin theme, and enhance with guitar, maybe add flute, and so on. Luckily these are all well orchestrated. The opener and closer seem to hit highest on the sustainability index, along with "Siipirikon Lento" (flight of the bird with the injured wing). More would emerge in the subsequent decade, with a few dramatic changes, so this is not one of those debuts that unwittingly doubled as a swan song. Mildly recommended, but more enthusiastically for certain listener profiles.
items._genre: progressive folk / jazz fusion / instrumental
items._cn_summary: 这是一张纯器乐的前卫民谣专辑，以小提琴与吉他为主导，配以长笛等配器，整体风格带有爵士化的即兴色彩，但走的是有结构、有纪律的jam路线而非自由即兴。乐评人将其与King Crimson的某些特质做类比，但指出其民谣根基更接近Talisma、Steve Hackett学派及芬兰同侪Aquaplan的作品。编曲上以吉他动机配合小提琴主题，辅以长笛点缀，形成循环往复的拼贴结构。评论认为各曲目之间略显雷同，缺乏足够辨识度，但开篇与终曲以及《Siipirikon Lento》在持续性上表现最佳。作为乐队的早期作品，它奠定了后续发展的基础。整体而言，这是一张制作工整、面向前卫民谣爱好者的专辑，但创新性有限，融合元素尚未充分展开。

items.body: Review by bandtutu — Drowning Steps - The Bravery of a Tireless Mind: Book One1. The Angels and the PlaygroundThe Angels and the Playground is an excellent introduction to the album. I really like the way it begins to develop the character's story. One detail I particularly love is the sound of the pencil writing on paper. It may seem like something simple, but it really adds to the immersion in the narrative. Caio's vocals also deserve praise, as they fit the song's concept very well and help convey the emotions behind the story.The first three minutes are beautiful. The acoustic guitar is very well crafted, and the atmosphere at the beginning reminds me of moments from "The Moon Touches Your Shoulder" by Porcupine Tree and "A Pillow of Winds" by Pink Floyd. There is a nostalgic tranquility to this introduction that I really enjoy, with a delicate arrangement that allows each element to find its own space. The song progresses naturally, without rushing, and never becomes tedious.Around 4:15, we get an incredible transition. The guitar riff, accompanied by the keyboards and synthesizers, changes the whole dimension of the composition and creates one of the first major moments of the song. I really like how these elements complement each other. The acoustic guitar picking that comes in here, breaking up the rhythm, also deserves praise.At 6:30, the distorted guitar introduces a section that, although I understand its importance to the narrative and the character's emotional context, buy simply doesn't work for me. I really don't like the riff. I understand the intention behind the change and recognize its purpose within the song, but I feel another approach could have conveyed the same feeling in a better way. It's a very personal criticism, especially because the composition wins me back shortly afterward.At 7:37, another guitar riff comes in, accompanied by the synthesizer, and the result is excellent. The drums also deserve praise, as the changes in the groove give the composition more personality. I really like the bass's rich and distinctive tone, and for me, this combination works so well that it makes up for much of what bothered me in the previous section.At 9:07, after a very striking, almost ghostly break, the song moves into a section that reminds me of "Moonloop" by Porcupine Tree. Even though this is a relatively long passage, it never becomes tedious. The instrumental development keeps me interested and shows the band's ability to sustain extended sections without simply relying on the repetition of the same idea.At 10:47, a riff with a more metal feel begins to emerge. I can't quite define exactly what kind of sound it is, but I really like the change. It's the kind of riff I would even like to write myself, both because of its sound and the energy it carries. Just a few seconds later, at 11:02, another transition completely changes the emotional state of the song. The arrangement takes on a different dimension, setting the stage for one of my favorite moments of the track.The keyboards entering at 11:23 are simply incredible. The piano comes in with a very emotional quality, adding a special sensitivity to everything that had been building up until that point. This section really moved me, especially because of the way the instrument transforms the atmosphere without needing an exaggerated change in intensity. Thiago's work on the keyboards is fundamental here, showing how important his contributions are to the musical identity of both the song and the album.When everything seems to be heading toward a satisfying conclusion, the guitar comes back and creates a sudden shock that, interestingly enough, works very well for me. I don't see this choice as a problem, in fact, I really like the effect it creates.However, my biggest criticism comes right after that, at 12:27, when the previously used riff returns. I feel that bringing it back is unnecessary and slightly hurts the flow of the composition. In my opinion, the song had already found an interesting path toward its conclusion, and I didn't like going back to that idea.Still, I really like the grandiose effect created by the keyboards together with the vocals during the "Then we went up, then we went down" section. The combination has a lot of strength and fits the scale of the narrative, although the repetition of this passage became a little boring for me. The ending of the section, with the guitar delay, works well and sets the stage for the final part of the song.The final section is beautiful. After so many changes in intensity and instrumental passages, the song finally reaches a sense of peace that almost feels like a release. The atmosphere reminds me a lot of "Insurgentes" by Steven Wilson. It also gives me the same feeling of relief I get when "Raider II" ends and "Like Dust I Have Cleared from My Eye" begins on Grace for Drowning. After such a long emotional journey, it feels like you can finally breathe.Despite some choices that don't completely work for me, "The Angels and the Playground" is a very strong opening, with excellent instrumental moments, engaging dynamic shifts, and an atmosphere that contributes just as much to the musical experience as it does to the narrative.------------------------------------2. Fragments of a LifetimeI found this song quite interesting, especially because it takes a very different approach from the previous track. It has this kind of progressive folk-ballad feel, with a very atmospheric arrangement. The keyboard effects also remind me a lot of "Entangled" by Genesis, and I think they fit the song really well.I also really liked the ending, when the song starts to give you the feeling that something is going wrong. It's an interesting choice because it works as a lead-in to the next track, "The Nod", leaving a certain sense of tension in the air.I like the idea behind the lyrics, especially this moment where the character is searching for peace. Overall, it's a simple track, but it works really well within the story of the album. --------------------------3. The NodThe beginning of this song reminds me a lot of Opeth atmosphere. Then a very distinctive guitar riff comes in. I wouldn't necessarily say it's good or bad, but I understand the idea behind it and I think it works.I really like the part around 2:35, when a sequenced drum pattern starts playing in the background. I thought that was a very interesting choice, and it reminds me of some things Wilson has done. The drums also deserve some praise here; they give the song a lot of dynamics and help build that sense of tension without simply making everything heavy all the time.The bass solo is also really good, especially with the character's narration playing in the background. Then the heavy guitar riff from the beginning comes back, and this time I think it really gains more meaning and fits the song very well.I also really liked the synthesizer solo, which brings a different texture to the track. The guitar solo is good as well and works nicely within the composition.Overall, I think the song takes its time to show this depth and develop the idea further.----------------------------------------------4. Waiting for RedemptionThis is easily my favorite song on the album. It starts with a piano in the background and Caio's vocals, which once again deserve a lot of praise. I really like how the song gradually builds along with the lyrics, creating more and more tension as it progresses.The way the song keeps building gives me a strong Neal Morse vibe. I can't really say whether it reminds me more of Transatlantic, Spock's Beard, or his solo work, but there is definitely something about the way the song develops that makes me think of those bands.Around 3:50, a guitar riff comes in and fits the song really well. The effects also deserve a lot of praise here. They manage to create a completely different atmosphere and then return to the previous one in a very natural way, without making the transitions feel forced.This particular riff really reminds me of a riff from the bridge of "Weenie Beenie," from Foo Fighters first album. It's not exactly the same, of course, but the way the riff comes in gives me a very similar feeling.Then, around 5:15, the song goes through a complete change. Once again, it shifts into a darkness and more introspective atmosphere.Shortly after that, the synthesizer solo comes in, and together with the drums, it sounds incredible. Listening to it gives me a really good feeling, almost as if I'm going on a trip. And maybe that's exactly what the character is experiencing in the story as well.Then that heavy riff comes back, this time accompanied by a wah-wah guitar solo, and I absolutely love it. It's really spectacular. The combination of the riff, the guitar tone, and the wah-wah works incredibly well.A new verse then comes in, very well placed, followed by the return of that almost ghostly section, which keeps repeating.My only real criticism is that this final part starts to feel a repetitive. I like the atmosphere it creates, but I think it goes on a little longer than it should.Even so, this is easily the track that stands out the most to me. It has so many great ideas that fit together really well, and the way it moves between different atmospheres while maintaining the narrative is excellent.----------------------------5. Life Handed Me the MapThis is the song that closes the album. It feels like the character is expressing his gratitude for having finally found the path; the "map", that will allow him to reconnect with the fragments of his past.I really like the effects and the atmosphere of the song. There is something very calm and reflective about it, which makes it feel appropriate as the ending of the story.I also really like the detail of hearing him write again at the end of the song, followed by the sound of the book closing. I think it's a great way to bring the album to an end, especially because the sound of the pencil writing appeared earlier in the story. It gives the whole thing a feeling of closure, almost as if we've just finished reading the character's story ourselves.--------------Overall Opinion on the AlbumFor me, this is a work that shows how much the band has matured, both in their songwriting and in the way they tell their story. I really enjoyed the songs, especially the way the album manages to create different atmospheres and make them work within the narrative.The main highlights for me were The Angels and the Playground, The Nod, and especially Waiting for Redemption. Overall, this is an album that really surprised me and shows how much Drowning Steps has evolved. It's a record I definitely plan to listen to over and over again, because I feel like there are still a lot of details to discover.-----------My Ratings:4,3/5 8,6/10Congratulations for this excellent work.Caio Claro / vocals, acoustic guitar (1), guitars (2,5), Arrangements and Sound ManipulationFabricio Mendon�a / drumsLeonardo Gon�alves / bassMarcos Duran / guitars (1-4)Tiago Pierucci / keyboards, synthesizers, effects, organ, piano, Wah-Wah guitar (2), backing vocals (4), Arrangements and Sound ManipulationRobin Peachey / vocals (1)La�s Gonzalez / vocals (2)Erlend Viken / vocals (3)

items.body: Sydney-based producer Harry Klein released the single “Fleeting Moments” in 2026, a dark-pop track built from electronica, wave and witch house. The song centers on transience, and on learning to love what doesn’t last. “Fleeting Moments” runs 3:22 and carries a synthesized trumpet line, falsetto vocals and a glitch beat. The single adds to a run of 2026 releases that includes “Push and Pull,” “Only Ever Now,” “Dance Therapy,” “Sun Down” featuring Billsbry, “Wild Child” and “Refuge” featuring Just Jen. Klein is touring Europe with psych-jazz outfit Almost Toast and plans to release his second album, “On The Path,” in November 2026 after he returns to Sydney. Rex Pollard of Electronic Music Australia described Klein’s production in terms of the mood it builds: “It is clear to me that Klein contains excellent knowledge on formulating dystopian atmospheres with his production, encouraging listeners to exit reality and enter his dark, sinister worlds.” “Fleeting Moments” is available to stream on Spotify. About Harry Klein Harry Klein is a multidisciplinary artist based in Eora/Sydney who combines music production with visual artistry across audio/visual performances. His work moves through dark electronica, glitchy IDM beats and ambient textures. Klein released his debut album, “And Then There Was None,” in 2023. The record explores questions of relationships, community and social power, pairing experimental electronica and dance productions with melancholic pop songwriting. Three singles preceded it that year: “Running out of Time,” “Cut & Dirty” and “Accelerate,” followed later in 2023 by “Who Floats Above.” He has performed at Up Late at the Powerhouse Museum and the Brand X Artist Showcase, built an interactive sound installation at Wide Open Space Festival, played his festival debut at Waves Retreat Festival and collaborated with fashion label The Injury at Pitch Festival. Klein also works as Senior Technical Officer of Screen Arts and Photomedia at Sydney College of the Arts, where he teaches and mentors emerging artists. “Fleeting Moments” is the latest in a string of 2026 singles building toward “On The Path,” Klein’s second album, due in November 2026.
items._genre: dark-pop / electronica / witch house / wave / glitch
items._cn_summary: Harry Klein 来自悉尼，是一位多媒介艺术家，作品横跨暗黑电子、碎拍节奏与氛围音色的边界。新单曲以电子合成小号、假声演唱与碎拍为骨架，聚焦于事物转瞬即逝的主题。评论者指出其制作擅长构建反乌托邦氛围，引导听者脱离现实、进入阴郁的声场空间。Klein 的首张专辑探讨关系、社群与社会权力，将实验电子与舞曲结构融入忧郁流行写作中。此外，他还涉足视听现场表演与声音装置，跨越纯音乐制作范畴。2026 年的多首单曲为其即将发行的第二张专辑铺路，整体呈现一位在独立电子场景中持续探索的跨学科创作者形象。

items.body: New England goth and post-punk band Ghost Painted Sky released the maxi-single “Kissing Lions” on October 6, 2026. The release previews the band’s upcoming second full-length album, “Failure Blooms.” The maxi-single carries three tracks: the title song, a “Kissing Lions (Effervescent Remix),” and “My Words Are Not My Own,” a new track that leans toward the band’s synthpop influences. Lisa Wood wrote the lyrics and sings. David Strong plays guitar, bass, ebow, drums and programming, and synths, and co-wrote the lyrics. Michael Boudreau contributes additional guitar and Aurora Grabill plays violin on both versions of “Kissing Lions.” William Faith of Faith and the Muse mixed and mastered the title track at his own 13 Studio. The remix and “My Words Are Not My Own” were mixed by Strong and mastered by Faith at the same studio. Strong also made the cover art, a stylized still from the “Kissing Lions” video. Kissing Lions by Ghost Painted Sky Ghost Painted Sky described “Kissing Lions” in the release’s Bandcamp notes: “those mostly vain attempts to seize on anything that creates a fleeting feeling of being alive for a moment amid relentless waves of the humdrum, doldrums, and failure […] bad decisions that bite back and create further downward spirals.” Ghost Painted Sky also put out an official video for “Kissing Lions.” “Kissing Lions” is available now as a digital download and via streaming on Bandcamp. About Ghost Painted Sky Ghost Painted Sky began in 2014 as the solo studio project of David Strong, who released a self-titled debut EP that year. A second short EP, “The Shadows Breath,” followed in 2015, alongside the band’s first live shows. Lisa Wood joined on vocals in 2018, starting with the “Scars” EP and continuing on the group’s debut full-length album, “Flightless”. Wood has since become the band’s primary vocalist. The band appeared on several compilations through the early 2020s, including “The Unquiet Grave 2020” (Cleopatra Records, 2020), “33 Gothic Bands You Should Know, Volume 8” (Post-Gothic, 2021), “You Are Still Not Alone” (Darkness Calling, 2021) and “Goths For Sanctuaries – The Album!!!” (2023). It released the “Ephemeral Wake” EP in 2021, followed by the singles “Corridors” in 2022 and “Insomnia” in 2024. Ghost Painted Sky is now finishing its second full-length album, “Failure Blooms,” with new studio contributions from guitarist Michael Boudreau and longtime live keyboardist and violinist Aurora Grabill. “Sound and Fury,” the album’s first single, came out in late March 2026, also mixed and mastered by Faith at 13 Studio. “Kissing Lions” is the second single, with “Failure Blooms” expected later in 2026.
items._genre: goth / post-punk / darkwave / synthpop
items._cn_summary: Ghost Painted Sky 是来自新英格兰的哥特与后朋克乐队，2026年10月发布单曲EP《Kissing Lions》，为其第二张全长专辑《Failure Blooms》预热。EP收录三首作品：同名曲、混音版本以及偏合成器流行的新曲《My Words Are Not My Own》。歌曲主题围绕徒劳地抓住能带来短暂鲜活感的事物、失败与恶性循环。由William Faith在13 Studio混音，David Strong创作词曲并担任多乐器演奏，Aurora Grabill的小提琴为作品增添层次。作为厂牌Cleopatra Records等合辑的参与者，乐队有着稳定的暗潮领域输出，但整体仍属类型内的常规制作，缺乏显著的实验性突破或跨领域融合。

items.album: Martin Saint releases ‘Endless Bridge’

items.body: Montreal dark-alternative artist Martin Saint released the single “Endless Bridge” on October 6, 2026, as a standalone digital track on Bandcamp. Martin Saint wrote and arranged “Endless Bridge” himself and handled vocals and guitars. Julie Abel plays piano, Frank Bones plays drums and Jack Vignavong plays bass. The track was recorded at Martini Lounge, Indica Studio 24 and Studio Pacifique in Montreal by Frank Bones and Martin Saint, with assistance from Olivier René de Cotret. Frank Bones mixed and mastered the track and co-produced it with Martin Saint. Ursa Minor handled the sleeve photography and design. Endless Bridge by Martin Saint In the track’s Bandcamp notes, Martin Saint described the song as a love story told through departures and returns. “Endless Bridge is about as close to a love song as I’ll ever get, but there’s a bittersweetness to it. Beginnings, endings, renewals. It expresses faith in the future and letting go of forces holding us back, even if this may take a lifetime.” He pointed to two specific reference points for the track’s sound: “Musically, I wanted something that’d sound as epic as The Killing Moon or With or Without You, for example. Melancholy, foggy, but uplifting and catchy.” “Endless Bridge” is available now as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp, with a minimum price of $1.50. About Martin Saint Martin Saint is a solo artist based in Montreal, Québec. Before launching the project under his own name, he was the lead singer and second guitarist of the city’s indie-rock quartet The Ember Glows, active between 2019 and 2024. His solo material moves into darker, more atmospheric territory, with baritone, emotionally-charged vocals and poetic lyrics that he has linked to Bauhaus, The Mission, The Jesus and Mary Chain, Nick Cave, Leonard Cohen and The Doors. “Endless Bridge” follows “Seekers,” Martin Saint’s fifth release under the solo name, out April 18, 2025. The ten-track album was recorded and mixed in Montreal at the Martini Lounge and Orange Studio by Martin Saint and Frank Bones, who also mastered it, with guest contributions from Julie Abel on piano, Delphine Dupont on lead guitar and backing vocals, Kevin Hills on bass, Hugo Joyal on pedal steel and Ursa Minor on backing vocals and artwork. His catalog also includes the albums “One Word Away,” “Fly Tales” and “Radio Murmurs,” along with the singles “Last Lights,” “The Law” and “I’ll Be Your Stranger,” featuring Ursa Minor. “Endless Bridge” carries the same core production team as “Seekers” into a new standalone single.

Liz Harris of Grouper draws up the anchor of her 2013 slowcore side project and sets sail once more with drummer Jed Bindeman on the high seas Linda's Head by Helen On 27th March 1980 Mt. St Helens erupted. Two months later, Liz Harris (AKA Grouper) was born. In 2013, she teamed up with drummer Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmon on bass, introducing the world to their shoegaze band Helen with the double A-side single ‘Felt This Way’ / ‘Dying All The Time’. Their dreamy debut The Original Faces followed two years after with the band subsequently laying dormant… until now. The reappearance of this Pacific Northwest slowcore trio a decade later is less an eruption, more a profusion. Or, better... The post Helen – Linda’s Head appeared first on The Quietus.

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Section X" is the second full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act BeyondTwilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works of another band). The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in March 2005. It�s the successor to "The Devil's Hall of Fame"from 2001. The nucleus of the band is intact (namely keyboard player and band founder Finn Zierler,guitarist Anders Ericson Kragh, bassist Anders Lindgren, and drummer Tomas Fred�n) since the releaseof "The Devil's Hall of Fame" but there have been a couple of lineup changes. The omnipresent JacobHansen (Invocator, Anubis Gate, Pyramaze...etc.) has joined on guitars and vocals, and American leadvocalist Kelly Sundown Carpenter (Darkology, Inner Sanctum, Outworld...etc.) has replaced Norwegianvocalist J�rn Lande (Ark, Masterplan, Allen - Lande...etc.).Stylistically the material on "Section X" is a combination of epic power metal and heavy metaloriented progressive metal. The latter means that this is progressive oriented music but nottechnical for the sake of it, and you shouldn't expect long instrumental sections dominating thetracks. Beyond Twilight�s music is more song oriented and generally features relatively accessibleverse/chorus structures. The tracks are quite sophisticated though (listen to the almost theatrical"Sleeping Beauty"). The closest relative is to my ears Symphony X because of the power metal andprogressive metal hybrid style, but also because of the epic nature of the music, the heaviness ofthe music (this is not vanilla Euro power metal), and the omnipresence of keyboards. Carpenter isquite the impressive singer with a strong voice and commanding delivery and the musicianship isgenerally through the roof on this release."Section X" features a powerful, heavy, and detailed sound production. It�s polished and wellproduced but still heavy and raw enough not to become too sterile sounding. Every instrument andvocal part stand out in the mix and are perfectly balanced. Just because this is Zierler�s projectdoesn�t mean that the keyboards overshadow everything else. On the contrary Zierler is veryconscious in terms of when his keyboards should dominate a track and when they shouldn�t. Uponconclusion "Section X" is a step up in quality from the already great "The Devil's Hall of Fame" andit�s just through and through a high quality release from Beyond Twilight. A 4 - 4.5 star (85%)rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦乐队Beyond Twilight的第二张全长录音室专辑，延续了乐队创始人兼键盘手Finn Zierler主导的核心阵容，并引入了吉他手Jacob Hansen与美国主唱Kelly Sundown Carpenter替代了此前的挪威歌手Jørn Lande。专辑风格被定位为史诗力量金属与重金属取向的前卫金属混合体，注重歌曲结构的可听性，编曲较为精致但不以冗长的器乐炫技为主导。键盘在作品中占据显著地位，与吉他形成层次丰富的对位，乐曲兼具力量感与沉重感。制作方面音色厚重饱满且细节清晰，各乐器与人声在混音中得以平衡呈现，乐评认为这是对前作的品质超越。乐评将其与Symphony X相提并论，强调其重型化与键盘主导的混合特质，整体属于较为标准的前卫金属范畴。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There are times when reality is stranger than fiction, and the story behind the making of this album is another example of that. Philippe DeBarge was a young French heir to a pharmaceutical fortune and a huge fan of The Pretty Things. Guitarist Dick Taylor had become disillusioned by the lack of impact of S.F. Sorrow, leading Victor Unitt to join the band as his replacement; this was the first album he recorded with them. DeBarge contacted the musicians and invited them to his opulent ch�teau in Saint-Tropez to propose a deal: he would fund their stay and record an album with himself as the lead vocalist. There, at the Epi-Plage club and his own residence, a thoroughly bohemian gathering took place, reminiscent of a Fran�oise Sagan novel; French rock legend Johnny Hallyday and actress Brigitte Bardot mingled and played guitar amidst a black-and-white "Nouvelle Vague" atmosphere. The album was recorded in London at Nova Studios. Thanks to DeBarge's funding, The Pretty Things had access to high-quality equipment, including an 8-track tape recorder.After the recording sessions, DeBarge took the masters to France, and the material remained in storage, unreleased and forgotten, on acetate discs. The acetate has been bootlegged since then. In 2010, it was acquired by Mike Stax, owner of the 1960s music magazine Ugly Things. He unearthed one of the two acetates, had it mixed and mastered, and then, as a bonus track, It led the classic Pretty Things lineup, which Dick Taylor had just left at the time the tracks with DeBarge were recorded, to record a song titled "Monsieur Rock" (Philippe's Ballad) as a bonus track for this release on Ugly Things UTCD-2207.The songs "Alexander," "Eagle's Son," and "It'll Never Be Me" were already known, having been recorded in the late 1960s by "Electric Banana", the pseudonym under which The Pretty Things recorded soundtracks for De Wolfe Music. Notably, these three songs appear in Menahem Golan's film What's Good for the Goose (1969).The Philippe DeBarge album itself serves as a bridge between the group's major Works, S.F. Sorrow and Parachute, yet it stands on its own merits. Less dark than its predecessor, it is perhaps the final example of that fresh, unpredictable, exciting, and thrilling, yet fun, psychedelia. This is evident in the opening track, "Hello, How Do You Do," which echoes the trippier side of the Rolling Stones' Their Satanic Majesties era, while the restrained calm of "You Might Even Say" recalls the Kinks. The track "Alexandre" is vocally challenging, raw and pugnacious, reminiscent of the early Who, yet it takes flight thanks to the Pretty Things' backing vocals and Victor Unitt's diverse guitar solos; these solos explore various shades of psychedelia while occasionally channeling the wild spirit of his previous group, the Edgar Broughton Band.These tracks sit alongside others with a more pop-oriented sound, charming thanks to the use of the clavichord, as in "Send You With Loving," and a prominent bassline. The album's real strength lies in its garage-rock, almost proto-punk, tracks, which are packed with energy and vocal harmonies, blending acoustic Indian ethnic elements with rock 'n' roll piano, as heard in "You're Running You And Me." "Peace" possesses a unique poetry and beauty, and is linked to "Eagle's Son," carrying forward its infectious rhythm and energy. It features melodies full of personality, where the rock and pop of "Swinging London" float through, almost becoming anthems of the era.While the influence of the Beatles could be traced in FS Sorrow, here we find psychedelia driven by acoustic guitar and harpsichord, punctuated by bursts of distorted electric guitar in soundscapes closer to the Kinks. The work evokes an era when the past and the future did not clash, simply because they were distinct, as seen in "New Day." Wally Waller handles piano and organ duties on "It'll Never Be Me", a track that remains laid-back right up until Victor Unitt's screeching solo, while the bongo percussion adds a relaxing touch that contrasts with the album's more urgent moments."Monsieur Rock (Ballad Of Philippe)" sounds more modern yet fits the spirit perfectly; it is even moving, evoking an era where the backing vocals and guitar seem to pick up exactly where they left off. The sound is raw, defiant, and powerful, with an improvisational feel, making it a fitting tribute that brings a sense of currency and relevance to this long-awaited official release.Twink left in late 1969 to form Pink Fairies. Skip Alan returned on drums just in time for the band's return to Abbey Road to begin work on Parachute, which retained the psychedelic sound but incorporated increasingly progressive elements. And Philippe DeBarge shines like those teenage memories that, as time goes by, leave you wondering if they were real or imagined...distorted like that very psychedelia, a time capsule that endures like the eternally fair weather of the Saint-Tropez coast.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Few late-80s metal albums are as influential as Savatage's fourth studio offering 'Hall of theMountain King', originally released by Atlantic. This is the first album by the American bandproduced by then-new producer Paul O'Neill, who had insisted on a more coherent musical direction,while also adding a bit of a conceptual edge to their recordings. At the same time, the band shows awillingness to experiment with more sophisticated arrangements and tighter compositions, as heardthroughout the album. The result is a darker, progressive-oriented record that sits at theintersection of melodic power metal and technical heavy metal, offering a triumphant and relentlesssound graced by fast-paced guitars and stunning vocal performances. As usual, fantastical elementsprevail on this Savatage album, bringing along an interesting aesthetic that sets the band apartfrom many of its contemporaries in the heavy metal scene. The lack of success of their previousalbums may have motivated Savatage to create a solid, kind of "bulletproof" collection of songs,that is what the record feels like.The straightforward songwriting, thunderous solos, and the overall dark atmosphere of 'Hall of theMountain King' render this album an appealing listen from start to finish. Its ten tracks areprimarily written by Jon and Criss Oliva, respectively lead singer and lead guitarist of the band,while a few songs also credit producer O'Neill as a co-writer. This record also has instrumentalarrangements of excerpts from 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' by Grieg and 'Mars, the Bringer ofWar' by Holst, which is further proof that Savatage were pursuing a sophistication of their soundwith this release. Opening side one is the song '24 Hrs. Ago'. Its sweeping, metallic riff providesa menacing and theatrical tone that is taken on by the following track 'Beyond the Doors of theDark', which is another really heavy and powerful composition. 'Legions' then explores a grooved uppower metal sound, while the melodic number 'Strange Wings' sees Savatage dialing back on the speedand aggression of the first three songs. Side two then follows up with the instrumental 'Prelude toMadness' and the iconic title track that needs no introduction. Of the four songs that follow andconclude the record, 'White Witch' and 'Devastation' impress as well-arranged ballsy metal pieces,while the instrumental interlude 'Last Dawn' is quite enjoyable. Of course, many of the progressiveelements are still underdeveloped on this release, while the instrumentals occasionally feel likestopgap entries in a sequence of songs mostly dedicated to powerful riffing and vocal bravado.Nevertheless, the vocals of Jon Oliva are fantastic all throughout 'Hall of the Mountain King',while the writing and the arrangements are really strong. The quality of the entire album isindicative of how Paul O'Neill understood what the band needed to become an 80s heavy metal majesty.And despite its minor imperfections, this 1987 record remains one of the most important entries inthe band's catalogue.
items._genre: progressive metal / heavy metal / power metal
items._cn_summary: Savatage第四张录音室专辑，Paul O'Neill首次担任制作人，将乐队推向更连贯、概念化的方向。专辑在旋律力量金属与技术重金属之间取得平衡，以快速吉他演奏与出色人声为核心，同时融入挪威作曲家格里格《山魔王的宫殿》与英国作曲家霍尔斯特《火星》选段的器乐改编，展现出对古典素材的引用意图。J. Oliva兄弟主导词曲创作，使整张作品呈现出统一的黑暗氛围与扎实编排。然而评论也指出，许多前卫元素在此阶段仍显稚嫩，部分器乐段落更像歌曲间的填充。O'Neill对乐队方向的把控被视为专辑品质的关键因素，使这张作品成为Savatage从早期走向成熟的转折点。

items.body: Independent Polish musician Sławek Stróżyk released the single “Tylko Ty” (“Only You”) on September 18, 2026, through distributor Crave Digital. The track places Polish-language male vocals in a synthwave/electro setting with a cyberpunk atmosphere, and explores closeness as a source of strength while the surrounding world changes. “Tylko Ty” runs 2 minutes and 47 seconds at 120 BPM. Stróżyk wrote the composition and lyrics, performed the track and handled its recording, production, mix and master himself in his home studio using Reaper. The original music and vocals involved no generative AI. “Tylko Ty” previously featured on the “Synthpop Symphony” podcast. The single is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. About Sławek Stróżyk Sławek Stróżyk is an independent musician, composer, guitarist, vocalist and producer based in Poznań, Poland, with more than twenty years of experience spanning session performance, recording engineering and sound design. His solo work brings together synthwave and electronic production with a wider interest in pop, ballads and rock. Stróżyk records in his own home studio using Reaper, taking responsibility for the complete creative and technical process from composition through to the finished master. “Tylko Ty,” released September 18, 2026, is his latest single under that approach. Stróżyk is currently working on his debut solo album, with material spanning pop, ballads, rock and synthwave, continuing the independent, self-produced method behind “Tylko Ty.”

items.body: Kontravoid released his new album “Sound Of The Void” on 2 October 2026 via Artoffact Records. The ten-track release is Cameron Findlay’s second full-length for the Toronto label, following 2024’s “Detachment.” Coldwave, EBM and electro run through the record. Side-Line covered the album’s announcement in September, when “Without” arrived as the first advance track. “Mortal” and “Chances” followed ahead of the full release. Sound Of The Void by Kontravoid The tracklist runs “Sound Of The Void,” “Without,” “Mortal,” “Subject,” “Chances,” “Dimension,” “Forever,” “Abandon,” “Returning” and “Phantom.” “Sound Of The Void” is available digitally and on CD, with a clear-vinyl first pressing also available on Bandcamp. About Kontravoid Kontravoid is the solo project of Canadian musician and producer Cameron Findlay, now based in Los Angeles. Before starting Kontravoid, he played drums with Crystal Castles in 2007 and 2008 and was a founding member of Toronto synth-pop band Parallels. His self-titled Kontravoid debut followed in 2012, released through the Minimal Wave label. He has toured North America alongside Buzz Kull, and the mask he wears on stage has become part of the project’s identity, a presence carried into “Sound Of The Void.”

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 《Vanishment》是Tiny Sun乐队的专辑，由Martina Sorbara、Jonathan Goldsmith与Don Rooke三人远程协作完成，十八首短小精致的曲目在三十四分钟内铺陈开来。专辑以原声吉他、尤克里里与滑棒吉他为底色，键盘点缀其间，配以Sorbara清澈高亢的声线。歌曲主题围绕失去——失去的爱情、失去的自信，以及对世界荒诞性的无奈接受。乐评指出作品呈现多样的风格渊源：开篇的矿工布鲁斯让人联想到Michelle Shocked，灵魂乡村气息的曲目呼应Cowboy Junkies的甜美管风琴质感，而某些曲目甚至带有Dolly Parton式的忧郁与颤音。评论特别称赞《A Grand Expanse》的精简编排，一分二十秒内以三十八个词完成表达。整体专辑如同梦境中的音乐，介于民谣与简约编曲之间。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢屠杀事件为主题，Sean Cooney联合Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等音乐人，通过原创歌曲重现这场英国工人阶级历史上的重要事件。专辑以书籍形式呈现，配以历史信件、政治漫画与插图，将音乐与历史文献结合成多媒体项目。歌曲聚焦于Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等普通人的故事，既有集会现场的期待与激动，也有骑兵冲击后的悲恸余波。Cooney的演唱富于情感，与两位出色歌手形成三重唱组合。在当下全球政府打压抗议的背景下，专辑被赋予了一层现实意义。整体而言，这是一张以历史叙事为核心的传统民谣作品，偏向英国工人阶级歌谣传统，在音乐实验性与跨界融合方面着墨不多。

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Crime of the Century is an album that manages to balance the accessibility of pop rock with elements of greater musical complexity. Although it is often associated with Progressive Rock, I see it more as a progressive pop rock album, using progressive elements without fully committing to the more complex characteristics of the genre. This is especially evident in tracks such as "School" and "Rudy", which feature more elaborate structures and development.One of the album's greatest strengths is precisely this balance between melody and sophistication. The songs are quite accessible, but they never feel simplistic. There is clearly a lot of attention to arrangements, dynamics and development, allowing the album to work both as a collection of great melodies and as a record with plenty of interesting musical details.Among the tracks, "School" is one of the major highlights, with an excellent combination of atmosphere, instrumentation and development. "Hide in Your Shell" is also one of my favorites and, in particular, one of the tracks that best represents what I find special about this album. "Bloody Well Right" and "Asylum" are also excellent, while "Dreamer", despite being a very good song, takes a more direct and accessible approach.The instrumentation is another strong point. The saxophone is particularly distinctive and contributes greatly to the album's identity. The keyboards also play an important role, although I find the saxophone more impressive overall. The drums are very well played, while the guitar and bass are effective without necessarily being the instruments that stand out the most.But the biggest vocal highlight is undoubtedly Roger Hodgson. His voice has a very distinctive character and is immediately recognizable. His high register and particular way of delivering melodies give Supertramp an identity that I find difficult to compare with other bands. The vocal melodies are excellent and are probably among the strongest aspects of the entire album. Rick Davies also delivers very good vocals, but Hodgson's voice is more memorable to me.The production has aged extremely well. The mixing is excellent, and the instruments are very clearly defined, allowing each element to be heard without difficulty. The album has a very balanced sound and still works remarkably well decades after its release. A particularly interesting production moment is the final section of "Asylum", which creates a very engaging atmosphere.I also consider the themes of the album to be important. There is a predominantly melancholic atmosphere connected to the human and social issues addressed throughout the songs. Subjects such as education, isolation and other recurring social problems appear in different forms. The title Crime of the Century itself can be interpreted as a criticism of the problems created by society and the kind of prison that society can impose on individuals.The cover reinforces this idea very effectively. The image of what appears to be a prison fits the atmosphere of the album and can be interpreted as a symbolic representation of society and the limitations it imposes. It is a cover that I consider extremely appropriate for the album's content.Despite its qualities, I do not consider Crime of the Century one of the greatest examples of Progressive Rock in the strictest sense of the genre. Its historical importance is significant, but I believe there are many albums that are much more progressive and representative of the genre. For this reason, I would not necessarily recommend it as an introduction to Progressive Rock. It can work very well as a bridge between rock/pop and progressive music, but there are bands with much more complex approaches and much stronger connections to the genre.I also do not consider the album particularly innovative in terms of progressive music, although it contains some interesting ideas and has a very strong individual identity. In fact, one of the most difficult things about it is finding other bands to compare it with, since Supertramp has a very distinctive sound of its own.Among its strongest points are the very well-defined instrumentation, especially the saxophone and keyboards, Roger Hodgson's vocals, and the themes behind the songs. I do not see many significant weaknesses in the album. My main reservation concerns the final tracks: although they are good, I find the first part of the album stronger and more memorable. "Crime of the Century", the title track, is the song that impresses me the least, although I still consider it a good composition.Overall, I consider Crime of the Century a very good album, with an excellent balance between accessibility, strong melodies, sophisticated instrumentation, distinctive vocals and social themes. The opening tracks, especially "School" and "Hide in Your Shell", are among its greatest highlights, and the production remains impressive.It is not, for me, an essential Progressive Rock album in the strictest sense of the genre, but it is a high-quality record with a very strong identity. Its ability to naturally combine pop rock with progressive elements is precisely what makes it special.
items._genre: progressive pop rock / art rock / crossover prog
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年的专辑试图在流行摇滚的可听性与渐进摇滚的复杂性之间寻找平衡。曲目如《School》和《Rudy》展示了较为精致的结构与编曲发展，萨克斯管的运用成为声音辨识度的核心，配以键盘、鼓与贝斯构建层次。Roger Hodgson的高音人声赋予乐队鲜明的个性，旋律写作是专辑最突出的优势。制作历经数十年仍保持良好的清晰度与平衡感。《Asylum》尾段的氛围营造尤为出色。专辑整体笼罩着忧郁的底色，探讨教育、孤立等社会议题，标题本身即是对社会规训的隐喻批评。封面视觉强化了批判主题。然而，这张作品本质上仍属于旋律驱动的流行摇滚范畴，带有渐进元素但未真正深入实验领域，对偏好前卫实验与即兴听法的听众而言，复杂性与冒险性较为有限。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Arguably one of the more radio-friendly hits from Dream Theater's 1994 album, 'Awake', 'Lie' is a groovy, riff-laden rocker that has some fantastic vocals and great instrumentation. After the success of 'Pull Me Under' a couple of years earlier, this track was probably the best choice for appealing to mainstream rock and metal fans, so its choice as a single is more than justified. Additional tracks include the ballads 'Space Dye Vest', which is keyboardist Kevin Moore's hauntingly beautiful swansong with the band, and one of many different recorded versions of 'To Live Forever', a song the band had played live for many years prior to this, but had never gotten around to recording a studio version of. As well as a live recording of 'Another Day', this is a pretty decent CD single for collectors and die-hard fans of the band.
items._genre: progressive metal / hard rock
items._cn_summary: 这首单曲发行于乐队1994年专辑时期，被视为最具主流亲和力的作品之一，风格偏groovy摇滚riff驱动的硬摇滚路线，人声与器乐表现扎实。评论指出这是继Pull Me Under之后打入主流市场的合理选择。单曲附赠Space Dye Vest这首键盘手Kevin Moore离队前的告别之作，氛围阴郁优美；另有To Live Forever的录音室版本与Another Day的现场录音。对于收藏者与铁杆粉丝而言，这张CD单曲有一定价值，但整体定位偏商业摇滚，与前卫实验路线相距较远。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Released in 2007 through the bands official fan club, 'Images and Words 15th Anniversary Performance' is literally what it says it is; Dream Theater playing the entire album that forever set the standard for all progressive metal bands to follow. Of course, it has its pros and cons. There's some interesting embellishments dotted around, which could keep us prog nerds at least somewhat invested for a little while, and it's cool to hear Jordan Rudess interpret some of Kevin Moore's keyboard parts. Then of course, there's vocalist James LaBrie. Sure, he struggles with some of it due to age and a well-documented vocal injury, but I guess at least he's trying. The band would go on to release a 25th anniversary performance of this album through their 'Lost Not Forgotten' series many years later, so, you know, it's probably slightly better than that one, again, due to LaBrie being another ten years older by then and struggling even more. Bless him. I don't think I'd ever choose to actually listen to this over the original 1992 studio album, which, for the record, is my favourite album of all time. But the name of this release describes exactly what you're getting here, so there's absolutely no point in taking it too seriously. It's a cool addition to the collection, and if you're a die-hard Dream Theater fan like I am, then you'll enjoy owning it. Simple as that.

items.body:
Clockenflap has unveiled its first wave of artists for 2026, with Hayley Williams, keshi, Slowdive, and Queens of the Stone Age among the names heading to Hong Kong.

The music and arts festival returns to Central Harbourfront Event Space from 4 to 6 December, bringing three days of live music, art, and activities to the city’s waterfront.

keshi will headline Friday, while Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams takes the Saturday headline slot with her solo show. Slowdive are confirmed to perform on Sunday.

The first announcement also features alternative R&B artist Malcolm Todd, South Korean indie favourites HYUKOH, Scottish alternative rock outfit The Jesus and Mary Chain, and Sonic Youth co-founder Kim Gordon.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Clockenflap (@clockenflap)

Elsewhere on the bill, DOMi & JD BECK and Bre kky Boy bring jazz explorations, while Digable Planets represent alternative hip-hop and Sleaford Mods deliver their distinctive post-punk sound. Electronic music fans can catch Marcel Dettmann and HE.R Soundsystem.

Also joining the line-up are singer-songwriter Daniela Andrade, New Zealand band SIX60, Thai artist pami, dream-pop act Fazerdaze, and genre-blending trio Chanpan.

Beyond its multiple music stages, Clockenflap will feature art installations, family-friendly workshops and performances, and food and drink from Hong Kong outlets, all set against the harbour and city skyline.

General ticket sales begin on 10 October at 3 PM HKT via Ticketflap. Ticket options are:

General admission, three-day weekend: HK$2,180

General admission, single day: HK$1,380

Under-18 admission, three-day weekend: HK$1,680

Eligible American Express cardmembers can access priority booking with 15% off tickets until 10 October at 2:59 PM HKT. They can subsequently enjoy 12% off tickets from the start of general sales until 10 November at 2:59 PM HKT, subject to terms and availability.

items.album: Beyond the headliners: 8 acts to discover at Singapore F1 Grand Prix 2026
items.excerpt:

Taking place from 9 to 11 October at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the race weekend also brings together Indonesian indie pop, Japanese guitar rock, British jazz and home-grown favourites.

items.body:
JJ Lin, The Killers and Lana Del Rey headline this year’s Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix, but there’s plenty more music to explore across the circuit. Taking place from 9 to 11 October at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the race weekend also brings together Indonesian indie pop, Japanese guitar rock, British jazz and home-grown favourites.

Whether you’re after an afternoon dance session or a band to add to your daily rotation, here are eight acts worth making time for between the racing action and headline sets.

Coldiac

When: 9 October, 9.30PM to 10.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Indie pop, R&B and synth-pop

Indonesian trio Coldiac make an appealing case for staying out a little longer. Their music brings together pop hooks, R&B influences and synths, offering plenty for listeners who like their indie pop with a groove.

Tracks such as ‘Wreck This Journal’ and ‘TARA’ helped introduce the band, whose catalogue has since expanded to include Lemons Made Lemonade and singles ‘Eksplorasi’ and ‘Jangan Pernah Berubah’. Their 2025 EP Loving You Like This also sees them put their own spin on Indonesian classics. For newcomers, that mix of original material and reinterpretations offers several routes into their sound ahead of Friday’s set.

KIKI

When: 10 October, 6PM to 6.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Synth-pop, nu-disco and dreamy dance music

Bangkok trio KIKI make music for anyone who likes a little introspection with their dancing. Their sound moves between guitar pop, funk, nu-disco and electronic textures, pairing reflective songwriting with rhythms that keep things moving.

Singapore listeners may recognise them from Baybeats, while their festival appearances also include Japan’s Fuji Rock and France’s Les Escales. Get acquainted through Post Existential Crisis or Death of a Daisy & Birth of an Oyster, then check out this year’s ‘Wait a Minute’. Their Saturday evening slot makes them a tempting stop for fans looking to explore Thailand’s indie scene.

Ezra Collective

When: 10 October, 3.45PM to 4.30PM

Where: Downtown, Zone 4

For fans of: Jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and a proper dance session

Bring your dancing shoes for Ezra Collective. The British quintet’s music draws jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and soul into performances built around rhythm and collective movement. Their album Where I’m Meant To Be earned them the Mercury Prize, and they bring that expansive sound to an early Saturday set.

Dance, No One’s Watching is a particularly good introduction to their approach. Try ‘God Gave Me Feet for Dancing’ and ‘Ajala’ before heading down. Drummer Femi Koleoso has spoken about shaping the band’s music around the momentum of a dance floor, and that spirit carries into their live shows, where getting the audience involved is central to the experience. Arrive ready to move.

Pleasantry

When: 10 October, 4PM to 4.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Dreamy indie music and intricate guitars

Singapore indie favourites Pleasantry reward those who listen closely. The quintet’s appeal lies in the interplay: guitars winding around each other, shifting rhythmic patterns and warm melodies that give their intricate arrangements an inviting centre.

Since Synapses, they’ve remained active on the gig circuit, taking their music overseas and letting songs evolve through years of performances. Their 2025 album Slow Burn captures that patient approach, but the real draw here is catching those musical conversations onstage. Try ‘Constellation’ and ‘Quiet’ before heading down, then listen for how the individual parts come together.

Lola Amour

When: 11 October, 4.30PM to 5.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Funk-pop, Filipino indie and communal singalongs

You may already know ‘Raining in Manila’. Sunday is your chance to get better acquainted with Lola Amour, the Manila band behind it and fellow favourite ‘Fallen’. Their mix of pop, funk and rock makes them an accessible starting point for anyone looking to explore contemporary Filipino music.

There’s plenty of evidence that their songs come into their own with a crowd. At shows previously covered by Bandwagon, fans have sung back lyrics, joined in with ad-libs and jumped through instrumental breaks. ‘Raining in Manila’ even brought the band onstage with Chris Martin during Coldplay’s Philippine visit in 2024. Come with the chorus learnt, and leave with a few more songs to look up.

TOKiMONSTA

When: 9 October, 3.15PM to 4.15PM

Where: Barge Stage, Zone 1

For fans of: Electronic music, R&B and adventurous production

TOKiMONSTA gives Zone 1 ticketholders a reason to arrive early on Friday. The GRAMMY-nominated producer’s catalogue stretches from Midnight Menu to Eternal Reverie, bringing electronic experimentation into conversation with R&B and a wide range of collaborators, including Anderson .Paak, Yuna and ZHU.

For a taste of that range, start with Eternal Reverie. Its tracks move through disco-pop, soul and quieter instrumental passages, with ‘Lucky U’ and ‘On Sum’ offering two very different entry points. That breadth makes her an intriguing pick for listeners who enjoy following a producer across genres.

Polkadot Stingray

When: 11 October, 6.45PM to 7.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Japanese rock and nimble guitar work

If guitar bands are your priority, put Polkadot Stingray on your list. Led by vocalist and guitarist Shizuku, the Japanese quartet have built their identity around tightly arranged rock songs, sharp guitar work and an assertive stage presence.

‘Telecaster Stripe’ and ‘Electric Public’ are useful starting points before their Sunday appearance. Shizuku also takes a central role in the band’s songwriting, design and video production, giving listeners a whole visual world to explore alongside the music. At the circuit, though, the draw is straightforward: a chance to hear those intricate arrangements delivered live.

Momocurly

When: 9 October, 5.45PM to 6.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: City pop, jazz and atmospheric indie

For a discovery that might take you somewhere unexpected, try Momocurly. The Tokyo-based French-Japanese duo bring together city pop, jazz, indie pop and ambient sounds, drawing on both Tokyo’s underground music scene and French influences.

They also handle the entire recording process themselves, from writing and performing to mixing and mastering. Their music’s combination of grooves and spacious textures makes this a promising pick for listeners who enjoy the softer, dreamier corners of pop. Catch them on Friday evening and give yourself 45 minutes to settle into their world.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by FORMULA 1 SINGAPORE GRAND PRIX (@f1nightrace)

Tickets can be purchased through the official Singapore Grand Prix website. Check that your ticket covers the day and access zone of your chosen performances. Plan accordingly and consult the official entertainment schedule before heading down.

items.body: Review by Aussie-Byrd-Brother — Not all prog-related albums need to hold overly complex arrangements, a new case in point being 2026's `Trauma', the sixth disc from frequent Yes/Asia keyboardist Geoff Downes DBA (Downes Braide Association) project that sees him teaming up with pop/rock vocalist, song-writer and producer Chris Braide. The latter's work (check out the eclectic smorgasbord of pop artists the guy has worked for!) results in a series of highly melodic, catchy and sophisticated pop/rock/AOR tunes here all given light prog-rock embellishments, the duo backed up by frequent DBA contributor, bassist Andy Hodge, drummers Ashley Soan (Rick Wakeman) and Tim Weller (The Oscillation), and multi-instrumentalist Dave Bainbridge (Iona).In Chris Braide's own words, the album is described as being "about the ghosts we inherit, the wounds we hide, and the light that still finds its way through. In the end, it is not an album about suffering, but survival. 'Trauma' isn't an album about defeat - it's about what happens after. It's about carrying your scars with dignity, refusing to be diminished, and remembering that kindness and perseverance ultimately outlast cruelty and fear." Despite the recurring theme, lower that raised eye-brow, prog fan, and step away from the Roger Dean cover, this ain't no concept album! But many of the tunes take a similar approach, displaying fancy pop-smarts with rousing choruses, soaring harmonies and crisp instrumental touches. A softer and less bombastic Asia might be a gentle comparison, although the tunes are more reflective, even if they both share a `radio friendly' approach (if popular radio was actually taking a chance on songs like this these days!).Looking at some of the highlights, after an Asia-esque fanfare, poppy opener `Hello, Hello' unveils a catchy recurring chorus and gliding harmonies, Chris Braide's voice revealing a charismatic rasp. The title track, one of the longer pieces at over eight minutes, is certainly one of more dramatic moments with its reassuring words, dreamy guitar strains and thoughtful piano dancing around shifting tempo changes, and is bound to be considered an album standout.The sweet and upbeat `Wonderland' slinks with programmed beats, jangling guitars, purring synths and a buoyant chorus that wouldn't be unexpected from any of the country rockers that are currently very popular. While not quite a duet, `Love and Loss' has Chris complimented vocally by British-Australian singer-songwriter Emmi (Emily Joy Green) - think Sound of Contact's `Beyond Illumination' or `Time Stands Still' from Rush for a similar effect. The ear-worm chorus of `I Wish I'd Known' is dream-pop perfection, `Do You Remember?' could be an Eighties pop-era Genesis out-take (sounds like it could have easily ended up on `Duke' or `Abacab'), and Chris comes together with synth-pop icon Marc Almond on pressing lament `Juliet'.Most prog-fans will gravitate towards the longest track here at nearly fifteen minutes the most, and `Lake of Memories' is a slowly unfolding multi-part suite with recurring passages across a solid mix of gentle reflective moments and driving rock passages. Each reprise of the enlivening chorus grows in urgency and power, and the constantly elegant synth-orchestration, Andy Hodge's sweetly murmuring bass and weeping guitar soloing throughout reminds of UK proggers Pendragon at their romantic best. It pairs nicely with the thoughtful and moving closer `Wherever You are Now', an emotive paean to a former love with a triumphant end.`Trauma' is perhaps a little long at nearly an hour, some listeners may find the polished-to-perfection production to be impossibly clean and the progressive elements too subdued, but there's no denying there's an exemplary range of quality song-writing, warming vocals and tasteful playing from Downes, Braide and company on display here. Give it a few spins, and listen for how this gem reveals its strengths.Four stars - but if you're a stuffy prog-snob who can't accept anything even a little poppy, just take a half-point off and walk away! ;)

Records in the US, with WEA International handling distribution elsewhere. Recording took place in early 1986 at RG Jones Recording Studios in Wimbledon, south-west London. “Scoundrel Days” runs ten tracks and just under 39 minutes. Alan Tarney produced and mixed most of the album, while Magne Furuholmen and Pål Waaktaar self-produced “I’ve Been Losing You,” “Maybe, Maybe” and “Soft Rains of April.” Gerry Kitchingham engineered the sessions, with additional mixing by John Hudson. The tracklist runs “Scoundrel Days,” “The Swing of Things,” “I’ve Been Losing You,” “October,” “Manhattan Skyline,” “Cry Wolf,” “We’re Looking for the Whales,” “The Weight of the Wind,” “Maybe, Maybe” and “Soft Rains of April.” The album was preceded by the single “I’ve Been Losing You,” released on 22 September 1986, which reached number one in Norway and number eight in the UK. “Cry Wolf” followed on 24 November 1986 and reached the top five in the UK, Poland and Ireland. “Manhattan Skyline” was issued as a single in February 1987, peaking at number 13 in the UK. “Scoundrel Days” reached number one in Norway and number two on the UK Albums Chart, and was certified platinum in the UK, Germany, Switzerland, France, New Zealand and Norway. Rhino Records released an expanded two-disc edition on 6 July 2010, adding extended mixes, demos, B-sides and live tracks. About a-ha a-ha formed in Oslo, Norway, in 1982 as a trio of Morten Harket on vocals, Magne Furuholmen on keyboards and Pål Waaktaar on guitars. Warner Bros. Records signed the band, and a-ha released its debut album, “Hunting High and Low,” in 1985. The title track and “Take On Me” became international hits, the latter reaching number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in October 1985. The band returned to RG Jones Recording Studios in Wimbledon in early 1986 to record its follow-up, “Scoundrel Days,” released on 6 October 1986. a-ha continued with “Stay on These Roads” (1988), “East of the Sun, West of the Moon” (1990) and “Memorial Beach” (1993) before going on hiatus. The group reformed in the late 1990s and released “Minor Earth Major Sky” (2000), “Lifelines” (2002), “Analogue” (2005), “Foot of the Mountain” (2009), “Cast in Steel” (2015) and “True North” (2022). The current touring lineup adds Karl-Oluf Wennerberg on drums and Erik Ljunggren on keyboards, both since 2009, and Even Ormestad on bass since 2015. Forty years after its release, “Scoundrel Days” remains the second entry in a catalogue that now spans eleven studio albums.

items.excerpt: 会期：2026/08/07〜2026/08/23 東京芸術劇場 シアターイースト［東京都］ 作・演出：岡田利規 公式サイト：https://www.geigeki.jp/performance/theater412/ 誰が舞台に立ち、誰が客席に座るのか。誰が誰を表象し、誰がそれを観るのか。『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』（作・演出：岡田利規）はそんな問いを改めて劇場へと持ち込み、そして観客に持ち帰らせるような作品だった。同作は岡田の東京芸術劇場舞台芸術部門芸術監督に就任第1作として上演されたもの。もともとはドイツのハノーファー州立劇場のレパートリーとして書かれ、5月に初演を迎えた岡田の現時点での最新作『Sliding Away』を、日本版の出演者・スタッフとともに新たに創り上げたものでもある。 タイトルが示す通り、舞台は映画を撮ろうとしているゾンビたちの撮影現場で展開する。登場するのは映画監督ゾンビのぽいぽい（東宮綾音）、俳優ゾンビのいいね（百瀬葉）、第5助監督ゾンビのまーしー（島田桃依）、第6助監督ゾンビのがーしー（石川朝日）、ゾンビ音楽家のげりま（福原冠）。しかし劇中で実際に映画の撮
items.body: 会期：2026/08/07〜2026/08/23 東京芸術劇場 シアターイースト［東京都］ 作・演出：岡田利規 公式サイト：https://www.geigeki.jp/performance/theater412/ 誰が舞台に立ち、誰が客席に座るのか。誰が誰を表象し、誰がそれを観るのか。『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』（作・演出：岡田利規）はそんな問いを改めて劇場へと持ち込み、そして観客に持ち帰らせるような作品だった。同作は岡田の東京芸術劇場舞台芸術部門芸術監督に就任第1作として上演されたもの。もともとはドイツのハノーファー州立劇場のレパートリーとして書かれ、5月に初演を迎えた岡田の現時点での最新作『Sliding Away』を、日本版の出演者・スタッフとともに新たに創り上げたものでもある。 タイトルが示す通り、舞台は映画を撮ろうとしているゾンビたちの撮影現場で展開する。登場するのは映画監督ゾンビのぽいぽい（東宮綾音）、俳優ゾンビのいいね（百瀬葉）、第5助監督ゾンビのまーしー（島田桃依）、第6助監督ゾンビのがーしー（石川朝日）、ゾンビ音楽家のげりま（福原冠）。しかし劇中で実際に映画の撮影が行なわれることはない。ゾンビたちは現場に集まったはいいものの、主要な俳優もスタッフもやってこないため撮影をはじめられない状況にあるのだ。かくして、時間を持て余したゾンビたちはゾンビが映画を撮ることに関する持論を交わしはじめる。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：銀色なつみ］ 冒頭からいいねは、ゾンビが人間を演じるための人間メイクをするのには3時間45分もかかる一方、「人間がゾンビになるときのメイクはもっとずっと短時間でテキトーに済ませたってオッケーってされてるんだから」その非対称性には許しがたいものがあるとぶち上げる。あるいはぽいぽいは「どうしてわれわれゾンビがわれわれゾンビのこと考えるのに人間のつくったゾンビ映画参照しなきゃいけないのか」と言い、「人間のゾンビ表象からわれわれ自由になれる日がいつしかくるようにと願って」「ゾンビの視点で描くゾンビ映画」をつくろうとしているのだと宣言する。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 非対称性というキーワードからも明らかなように、ここではゾンビの存在が現実世界におけるさまざまなマイノリティと重ね合わせられている。劇中に登場するゾンビという言葉の大半は、そのまま例えばクィアという言葉に置き換えても──「クィアの視点で描くクィア映画」というようなかたちで──成立するだろう。言及される問題は多岐にわたる。例えばゾンビが登場する映画はすべてがゾンビ映画という括りに入れられてしまうということ。ゾンビは本当は人間と同じように歩くのであって「人間のゾンビ表象」は間違っているということ。残念ながらそんな「人間のゾンビ表象」によってゾンビが「教育」されてしまっている側面もあるということ。しかし「問題は人間の映画監督のゾンビ描写が貧しいってこと」ではなく「ゾンビの映画監督が圧倒的に少なすぎるっていうのが問題のほんとの所在」であるのだということ等々。 そして話題は観客のことにも及ぶ。ゾンビの観客はどれくらいいるのかと。しかもこの問いは、劇場にいる観客に向けて発せられるのだ。さらに舞台上のゾンビたちはおもむろにゾンビメイクを拭い去り、自分たちが「映画を撮りたいゾンビ」を演じる人間の俳優でしかないという身も蓋もない事実を観客に改めて突きつける。そうして明らかになるのは、舞台上にも客席にも、このゾンビについての演劇が上演されている劇場内にゾンビはひとりも存在していないという端的な事実だ。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：相模友士郎］ ともすればポリコレ的言説の演説会にもなりかねない（というかそうでなかったとはなかなか言い切れない）この作品が、チャーミングな飽きさせない上演として成立していたのは俳優たちの魅力に負うところが大きいだろう。そのようなかたちで問いを社会へと持ち込めることもまた、演劇の可能性のひとつなのだ。 この『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』という作品は、『消しゴム山』（初演：2019）から『リビングルームのメタモルフォーシス』（初演：2023）へと展開する脱人間中心主義を掲げた岡田の一連の作品のひとつとしても位置づけられるだろう。そのコンセプトは『消しゴム山』では例えば「モノのための演劇」というきわめてラディカルなかたちで実現されていたが、同作では再演を重ねるなかで、アクセシビリティをめぐるさまざまな取り組みも実施されてきたのだった。それは中心とされてきたはずの人間のなかにも周縁化された存在がいるのだという、当然でありながら日本の演劇界においては十分に目が向けられてこなかった事実に改めて目を向ける取り組みでもある。ノン・ネイティブ日本語話者を出演者に迎えた『宇宙船イン・ビトゥイーン号の窓』（初演：2023）もこの系譜に連なる重要な作品だ。 劇場で配布されていた『劇場に置くノート1』に岡田は次のように記していた。「舞台芸術の上演が現状よりももっと、観客の身体やその振る舞いが肯定されている場になる。観客の身体どうしがその存在を肯定し合っているという場になる。そしたらそれはイノベーションだとおもう。どうやったらそれは起こせるだろう」。このような思想は岡田がアーティスティック・ディレクターを務める舞台芸術祭「秋の隕石」のプログラムや体制にも持ち込まれている。2026年の「秋の隕石」は10月9日（金）から11月3日（火）にかけての開催を予定している。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 観賞日：2026/08/12（水） 関連記事 KYOTO EXPERIMENT 2023（前編） チェルフィッチュ『宇宙船イン・ビトゥイーン号の窓』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2023年11月15日号） チェルフィッチュ×金氏徹平『消しゴム山』（エクストラ音声「山がつぶやいている」／配信版『消しゴム山は見ている』）｜山﨑健太：artscapeレビュー（2021年04月15日号） 没入するモノたち──チェルフィッチュ×金氏徹平『消しゴム山』｜池田剛介：フォーカス（2019年10月15日号）

items._cn_summary: 这篇评论并非音乐乐评，而是日本剧作家岡田利規（chelfitchu）执导的舞台剧《映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇》的剧评。作品以僵尸拍摄电影的剧场为框架，探讨人类与僵尸之间的非对称性，并借此映射现实世界中少数群体被主流话语所表征的问题。剧中僵尸既是剧中角色，也被揭示为扮演僵尸的人类演员，以此打破舞台与观众席之间的界限。评论将本作品置于岡田自《消しゴム山》以来所主张的脱人类中心主义创作脉络中加以定位，指出其与无障碍化实践及多语言演出的关联。虽然评论内容详实且具有学术深度，但本文讨论对象为戏剧而非音乐，与用户的实验音乐、爵士、电子、暗潮等音乐口味基本无关。

items._cn_summary: Sam Smith暌违三年推出的第五张专辑，从前作的流行路线回归至接近早期作品的静谧、沉稳音色。整张作品融汇灵魂乐、福音、独立民谣与凯尔特元素，构建出优美的音世界。其中与Feist合作的'Moondance'是专辑核心亮点，以壮阔的编曲承载关于伴侣关系的细腻私密心象。整体风格偏向情绪化的人声演绎与抒情旋律，编曲氛围讲究但未走向实验或前卫领域，与用户的实验、前卫爵士及电子取向距离较远，信息量也较为有限。
